attributes.description: Description of any Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) requirements specified by the client for this opportunity (e.g., carbon targets, local content requirements, diversity commitments). Free-text field for BD qualification notes.
attributes.references: ISO 14001 Environmental Management; ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety; EPA

attributes.name: estimated_contract_value
attributes.description: Estimated total contract value of the opportunity in the reporting currency. Used for pipeline forecasting, revenue planning, and bid/no-bid decision thresholds. Raw commercial estimate; not a committed figure.
attributes.references: IFRS 15 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers); Salesforce CRM Opportunity Amount

attributes.name: expected_award_date
attributes.description: Anticipated date on which the contract is expected to be formally awarded to the company. Used for pipeline close-date forecasting and resource mobilization planning.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Opportunity Close Date; PMO Pipeline Forecasting Standard

attributes.name: expected_ntp_date
attributes.description: Anticipated date on which the client will issue the Notice to Proceed (NTP), authorizing the start of construction work. Used for resource planning and revenue recognition scheduling.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Opportunity; FIDIC Contract Conditions; IFRS 15

attributes.name: is_jv_bid
attributes.description: Indicates whether this opportunity is being pursued as a Joint Venture (JV) arrangement. True = JV bid; False = sole-entity bid. Drives JV governance and risk review processes.
attributes.references: FIDIC Joint Venture Guidelines; PMO JV Governance Framework

attributes.name: jv_partner_names
attributes.description: Names of Joint Venture (JV) partners with whom the company intends to bid on this opportunity. Relevant for JV-structured bids common in large infrastructure and EPC projects. Confidential commercial information.
attributes.references: FIDIC Joint Venture Guidelines; PMO JV Governance Framework

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the opportunity record in the source CRM system. Used for change tracking, data freshness monitoring, and incremental pipeline loads.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Opportunity LastModifiedDate; GDPR Article 5 (Data Accuracy)

attributes.name: leed_certification_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the client requires LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) certification for the project. True = LEED certification is a contract requirement. Drives sustainability planning and cost estimation.
attributes.references: LEED (U.S. Green Building Council); ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

attributes.name: loss_reason
attributes.description: Reason code or description explaining why the opportunity was lost or withdrawn (e.g., price, technical score, client relationship, competitor strength, scope mismatch). Populated when win_loss_outcome is 'lost' or 'withdrawn'. Used for BD lessons-learned and competitive intelligence. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: price|technical_score|client_relationship|competitor_strength|scope_mismatch|capacity|no_bid_decision|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Opportunity; PMO Win/Loss Review Process

attributes.name: next_action
attributes.description: Description of the next planned business development action required to advance this opportunity (e.g., 'Submit EOI by 15-Mar', 'Attend client briefing', 'Complete bid/no-bid review'). Operational field used by BD team for pipeline management.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Opportunity Next Step; PMO BD Pipeline Governance

attributes.name: next_action_due_date
attributes.description: Target date by which the next business development action must be completed. Used for BD pipeline hygiene, follow-up scheduling, and opportunity stagnation alerts.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Opportunity; PMO BD Pipeline Governance

attributes.name: opportunity_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the construction opportunity, typically including the project name and client name (e.g., 'Greenfield Highway Extension – ADOT'). Used for identification in pipeline reports and BD dashboards.

attributes.name: opportunity_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric identifier for the opportunity as assigned in Salesforce CRM. Used for cross-system reference and client-facing communications.

attributes.name: opportunity_status
attributes.description: Lifecycle status of the opportunity record indicating whether it is actively pursued, won, lost, on hold, or cancelled. Distinct from pipeline_stage which tracks the BD workflow step.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Opportunity Object; PMO Pipeline Governance

attributes.name: pipeline_stage
attributes.description: Current stage of the opportunity in the business development pipeline. Drives pipeline forecasting and BD reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: prospect|qualification|bid_preparation|submitted|negotiation|awarded|lost|no_bid — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Opportunity Stage; PMO Pipeline Governance

attributes.name: prequalification_status
attributes.description: Status of the company's prequalification with the client for this opportunity. Many public-sector and large private clients require formal prequalification before bid submission. Drives eligibility gating in the BD pipeline.
attributes.references: FIDIC Procurement Guidelines; PMO Prequalification Process

attributes.name: probability_of_win_pct
attributes.description: Estimated probability (0–100%) that the company will be awarded this contract. Used to calculate weighted pipeline value for revenue forecasting. Assigned by the BD owner and reviewed at stage gates.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Opportunity Probability; PMO Pipeline Forecasting Standard

attributes.name: project_duration_months
attributes.description: Estimated duration of the construction project in months from NTP to practical completion. Used for resource planning, revenue phasing, and schedule risk assessment.
attributes.references: Oracle Primavera P6 Project Scheduling; PMO Planning Standards

attributes.name: project_location_country
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the country where the construction project will be executed (e.g., USA, ARE, GBR). Used for geographic pipeline analysis and regulatory compliance scoping.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Country Codes; EPA; OSHA Jurisdictional Scope

attributes.name: project_location_region
attributes.description: State, province, or region where the construction project will be executed. Used for regional pipeline reporting, resource planning, and jurisdictional compliance (e.g., OSHA state plans, local building codes).
attributes.references: OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Administration); IBC (International Building Code)

attributes.name: project_type
attributes.description: Classification of the construction project type (e.g., highway, airport, bridge, power plant, residential, commercial, industrial). Used for market segmentation and capability matching. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: highway|airport|bridge|power_plant|residential|commercial|industrial|water_treatment|rail|data_center — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IBC (International Building Code); ASCE (American Society of Civil Engineers)

attributes.name: rfp_issue_date
attributes.description: Date on which the client issued the Request for Proposal (RFP) or Invitation to Tender (ITT). Marks the formal start of the bid preparation phase.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Opportunity; FIDIC Procurement Guidelines

attributes.name: rfq_number
attributes.description: Client-issued Request for Quotation (RFQ) or Request for Proposal (RFP) reference number. Used for cross-referencing with client procurement documents and Aconex correspondence.
attributes.references: Aconex Document Management; FIDIC Procurement Guidelines

attributes.name: sector
attributes.description: Sector classification of the client commissioning the work: public-sector (government/municipal), private-sector (developer/corporate), or PPP/BOT (public-private partnership or build-operate-transfer arrangement). Used for client segmentation and reporting.
attributes.references: PMO Client Segmentation Framework; IFRS/GAAP Revenue Recognition

attributes.name: source_crm_opportunity_code
attributes.description: Original opportunity identifier from the Salesforce CRM system of record. Used for data lineage, cross-system reconciliation, and traceability back to the operational source.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Opportunity Object; Data Governance Lineage Standard

attributes.name: strategic_priority
attributes.description: Internal strategic priority classification assigned to this opportunity by BD leadership. Tier 1 = highest strategic importance (must-win); Tier 2 = important but not critical; Tier 3 = opportunistic. Drives resource allocation for bid preparation.
attributes.references: PMO BD Strategy Framework; Salesforce CRM Opportunity

attributes.name: weighted_pipeline_value
attributes.description: Estimated contract value multiplied by the probability of win percentage, representing the risk-adjusted contribution of this opportunity to the revenue forecast. Key metric for executive pipeline reporting.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Opportunity; PMO Pipeline Forecasting Standard; IFRS 15

attributes.name: win_loss_outcome
attributes.description: Final outcome of the opportunity after the bid process concludes. Won = contract awarded to company; Lost = awarded to competitor; Withdrawn = company withdrew bid; No_award = client cancelled procurement. Drives win rate analytics and BD performance reporting.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Opportunity Stage; PMO Win/Loss Review Process

products.name: project_engagement
products.description: Bridge record linking a client account to a specific construction project they commission, sponsor, or fund. Captures client role (owner, co-sponsor, JV lead, funding agency, end-user), engagement start and end dates, primary client representative, contract reference, engagement status, and satisfaction indicators. SSOT for which clients are involved in which projects from the client domain perspective. Does not duplicate project master data owned by the project domain.

attributes.name: project_engagement_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the client project engagement record. Primary key for this bridge entity linking a client account to a specific construction project.

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the client account (owner, developer, sponsor, or funding agency) involved in this engagement. Links to the client master record.

attributes.name: agreement_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary contract governing this client-project engagement (e.g., EPC, FIDIC, GMP, DB, DBB, or PPP/BOT contract). Links to the contract master record.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Contract Administration; SAP S/4HANA – Project Systems

attributes.name: client_opportunity_id
attributes.description: The opportunity identifier from the Salesforce CRM system that tracks the sales pipeline record associated with this engagement. Enables traceability from opportunity pursuit through to active project delivery.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM – Opportunity Tracking; Pipeline Forecasting

attributes.name: construction_project_id
attributes.description: Reference to the construction project that this client is commissioning, sponsoring, or funding. Links to the project master record.

attributes.name: contact_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary contact person designated by the client to represent their interests on this project. Typically the client-side project manager or authorized representative.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM – Account Management; FIDIC – Contract Administration

attributes.name: framework_agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to client.client_framework_agreement. Business justification: Project engagements in construction are frequently executed as call-offs under a framework agreement or MSA. Linking project_engagement directly to client_framework_agreement enables reporting on fram

attributes.name: rfp_issuance_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to client.rfp_issuance. Business justification: A project engagement (the awarded contract relationship) originates from an RFP/ITT issuance. Linking project_engagement to rfp_issuance closes the BD pipeline loop: opportunity → RFP issuance → proje

attributes.name: advance_payment_amount
attributes.description: The value of any advance payment made by the client to the contractor at the commencement of this engagement, typically secured by an advance payment guarantee. Expressed in the contract currency.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Advance Payment; SAP S/4HANA – Accounts Receivable; IFRS 15

attributes.name: approved_variation_value
attributes.description: The cumulative value of all approved Change Orders (CO) / variations issued by the client on this engagement to date. Reflects the net adjustment to the original contract value due to scope changes.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Variation Orders; Procore – Change Orders; IFRS 15 – Contract Modifications

attributes.name: bid_reference_number
attributes.description: The reference number assigned to the original bid or tender submission (RFP/RFQ response) that led to this engagement being awarded. Links the engagement back to the opportunity pipeline in the CRM.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM – Bid Management; RFP/RFQ Standards

attributes.name: bim_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the client has mandated Building Information Modeling (BIM) as a contractual deliverable requirement for this engagement. Drives BIM execution plan obligations and Autodesk BIM 360 usage.
attributes.references: Autodesk BIM 360 – Design Collaboration; BIM Standards (ISO 19650)

attributes.name: client_role
attributes.description: The functional role the client plays in this project engagement. Distinguishes between the primary owner, co-sponsor in a joint venture (JV), lead JV partner, funding agency (e.g., government body), end-user of the completed asset, or developer. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: owner|co_sponsor|jv_lead|funding_agency|end_user|developer|ppp_authority|bot_concessionaire — promote to reference product if additional roles are needed]

attributes.name: communication_preference
attributes.description: The client's preferred channel for formal project communications and correspondence on this engagement. Determines how RFIs, submittals, transmittals, and official notices are delivered.
attributes.references: Aconex – Correspondence; Procore – RFIs; FIDIC – Contract Administration

attributes.name: contract_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the contract value and financial commitments in this engagement (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP, AED). Required for multi-currency project reporting and IFRS/GAAP compliance.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 – Currency Codes; IFRS/GAAP – Financial Reporting

attributes.name: contract_reference_number
attributes.description: The externally-known contract number or agreement reference assigned to the governing contract for this engagement. Used for cross-referencing with contract administration systems and client correspondence.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Contract Administration; SAP S/4HANA – Project Systems; Aconex – Document Management

attributes.name: contract_value
attributes.description: The total awarded contract value for this client-project engagement as agreed at contract execution. Represents the baseline financial commitment from the client. Expressed in the contract currency.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Contract Price; IFRS 15 – Revenue from Contracts with Customers; SAP S/4HANA – Finance

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp at which this client-project engagement record was first created in the system. Provides the audit trail creation marker for data governance and lineage tracking.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 – Record Management; GDPR – Data Governance

attributes.name: dispute_status
attributes.description: Current status of any formal contractual dispute between the client and the contractor on this engagement. Tracks the dispute resolution lifecycle from initial notice through negotiation, adjudication, or arbitration to resolution.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Dispute Resolution; Contract Administration Standards

attributes.name: dlp_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which the Defects Liability Period (DLP) expires, after which the contractor's obligation to rectify defects at no cost to the client ceases. Critical for contract close-out and final account settlement.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Defects Liability Period (DLP); ISO 9001 – Quality Management

attributes.name: engagement_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which the client's formal involvement in the project is expected to conclude or has concluded. Typically aligned with project handover, Defects Liability Period (DLP) expiry, or BOT concession end date. Nullable for open-ended engagements.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Defects Liability Period (DLP); Oracle Primavera P6 – Project Completion

attributes.name: engagement_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing qualitative notes, special conditions, or contextual information relevant to this client-project engagement that are not captured in structured fields. Used by account managers and project directors.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM – Account Management; Aconex – Correspondence

attributes.name: engagement_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference code assigned to this client-project engagement. Used in correspondence, transmittals, and CRM tracking to uniquely identify the engagement across systems.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM – Opportunity Tracking; Aconex – Correspondence

attributes.name: engagement_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which the client's formal involvement in the project commenced. Typically aligned with the Notice to Proceed (NTP) date or the contract execution date.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Contract Commencement; Oracle Primavera P6 – Baseline Management

attributes.name: engagement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the client-project engagement. Tracks whether the engagement is actively ongoing, pending formal commencement (awaiting NTP), on hold, completed at project handover, terminated early, or cancelled prior to commencement.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM – Pipeline Forecasting; Oracle Primavera P6 – Project Status

attributes.name: engagement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the contractual or commercial arrangement type governing this engagement. Reflects the delivery model: EPC (Engineering Procurement and Construction), Design-Build (DB), Design-Bid-Build (DBB), Public-Private Partnership (PPP), Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT), Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP), framework agreement, or direct award. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: epc|design_build|design_bid_build|ppp|bot|gmp|framework|direct_award — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FIDIC – Contract Types; PPP/BOT Frameworks; IBC

attributes.name: eot_days_granted
attributes.description: The total number of calendar days of Extension of Time (EOT) formally granted by the client to the contractor on this engagement to date. Adjusts the contractual completion date and affects LD exposure.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Extension of Time (EOT); Oracle Primavera P6 – Schedule Management

attributes.name: funding_source
attributes.description: Classification of the primary funding mechanism used by the client to finance this project engagement. Supports financial risk assessment and reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: government_grant|private_equity|bank_loan|bond_issuance|multilateral|internal_budget|mixed|ppp_concession — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: handover_date
attributes.description: The actual or planned date on which the completed project asset was or is expected to be handed over to the client. Marks the transition from construction to the Defects Liability Period (DLP) or Operations and Maintenance (O&M) phase.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Taking Over Certificate; ISO 9001 – Commissioning and Handover

attributes.name: hse_requirements_classification
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Safety and Environment (HSE) Requirements Classification
attributes.description: Classification of the HSE (Health, Safety and Environment) requirements imposed by the client for this engagement. Reflects the risk profile and regulatory environment: standard (baseline OSHA/ISO 45001), enhanced (client-specific elevated requirements), or critical (high-hazard environments such as nuclear, offshore, or major infrastructure).
attributes.references: OSHA – Occupational Safety; ISO 45001 – OHS Management; Intelex – HSE Management

attributes.name: insurance_compliance_verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the contractor's required insurance policies (e.g., professional indemnity, public liability, contractor's all-risk) have been verified as compliant with the client's contractual requirements for this engagement.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Insurance Requirements; ISO 45001 – Occupational Health and Safety

attributes.name: jv_participation_percentage
attributes.description: The client's ownership or participation share percentage in a Joint Venture (JV) arrangement for this project. Applicable when the client role is co-sponsor or JV lead. Null for sole-owner engagements.
attributes.references: JV Agreement Standards; IFRS 11 – Joint Arrangements; FIDIC

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp at which this client-project engagement record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking, data freshness monitoring, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver layer.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 – Record Management; GDPR – Data Governance

attributes.name: leed_certification_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) Certification Required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the client has mandated LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) certification for the project deliverable as a contractual requirement in this engagement.
attributes.references: LEED – U.S. Green Building Council; ISO 14001 – Environmental Management

attributes.name: liquidated_damages_rate
attributes.description: The contractually agreed daily or weekly Liquidated Damages (LD) rate payable by the contractor to the client in the event of project delay beyond the agreed completion date. Expressed in the contract currency per day.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Liquidated Damages (LD); Contract Administration Standards

attributes.name: ntp_date
attributes.description: The date on which the Notice to Proceed (NTP) was formally issued by the client to the contractor, authorizing commencement of construction works. A critical contractual milestone in the engagement lifecycle.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Contract Administration; Procore – Change Orders

attributes.name: performance_bond_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the client has required the contractor to provide a performance bond as a financial security instrument for this engagement. Affects contract financial structuring and risk management.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Performance Security; Contract Administration Standards

attributes.name: procurement_method
attributes.description: The procurement route used by the client to award this engagement. Indicates whether the contract was awarded through open tender, selective tender, direct negotiation, Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or a framework call-off.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Procurement; Salesforce CRM – Bid Management; RFP/RFQ Standards

attributes.name: relationship_tier
attributes.description: Segmentation tier assigned to this client engagement based on strategic importance, revenue contribution, and long-term relationship value. Drives account management priority and resource allocation.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM – Account Management; CRM Best Practices

attributes.name: repeat_client
attributes.description: Indicates whether this client has previously engaged the construction company on one or more prior projects. Supports client relationship analytics, win-rate reporting, and strategic account management.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM – Account Management; CRM Best Practices

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: The agreed frequency at which formal project progress reports are submitted to the client for this engagement. Governs the reporting cadence for schedule, cost, and HSE performance updates.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Contract Administration; Oracle Primavera P6 – Progress Tracking

attributes.name: retention_percentage
attributes.description: The contractually agreed retention percentage withheld by the client from each progress payment as a performance security. Typically released in two tranches: at practical completion and at DLP expiry.
attributes.references: FIDIC – Retention Money; SAP S/4HANA – Accounts Payable; IFRS 15

attributes.name: satisfaction_score
attributes.description: Numeric score representing the client's satisfaction with the construction company's performance on this engagement, typically captured through formal client satisfaction surveys. Scored on a standardized scale (e.g., 1.00–5.00 or 0.00–10.00).
attributes.references: ISO 9001 – Customer Satisfaction; Salesforce CRM – Account Management

attributes.name: satisfaction_survey_date
attributes.description: The date on which the most recent client satisfaction survey was conducted for this engagement. Used to track the currency of satisfaction data and schedule follow-up surveys.

attributes.name: sector
attributes.description: Sector classification of the client for this engagement: public-sector (government/municipal), private-sector (commercial developer or corporation), or PPP (Public-Private Partnership arrangement). Supports client segmentation and reporting.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM – Account Management; IFRS/GAAP – Segment Reporting

products.name: rfp_issuance

attributes.name: rfp_issuance_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each RFP/RFQ/ITT issuance record in the system. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: client_account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the client/owner account that issued this solicitation. Links to the master client account record in the CRM. Sourced from Salesforce CRM Account Management.

attributes.name: client_opportunity_id
attributes.description: Reference to the linked sales opportunity in the CRM pipeline that this RFP issuance is associated with. Enables traceability from solicitation to bid pursuit. Sourced from Salesforce CRM Opportunity Tracking.

attributes.name: framework_agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to client.client_framework_agreement. Business justification: In construction, RFPs are frequently issued as call-offs under a pre-existing framework agreement or MSA. Linking rfp_issuance to client_framework_agreement enables traceability from a specific tender

attributes.name: addendum_count
attributes.description: The total number of addenda (amendments) issued by the client against this RFP since original issuance. Each addendum modifies the original RFP terms, scope, or schedule. Used to track document version history.
attributes.references: Aconex Document Management; FIDIC Procurement Guidelines

attributes.name: anticipated_award_date
attributes.description: The client's indicative target date for issuing the Notice to Proceed (NTP) or contract award, as stated in the RFP. Used for resource planning, bid team scheduling, and pipeline forecasting in Salesforce CRM.
attributes.references: FIDIC Procurement Guidelines; Oracle Primavera P6; Salesforce CRM

attributes.name: anticipated_completion_date
attributes.description: The client's required or indicative project completion date as stated in the RFP. Defines the overall programme duration and is a key input to CPM (Critical Path Method) scheduling and resource planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Primavera P6; FIDIC Procurement Guidelines; ASCE

attributes.name: anticipated_start_date
attributes.description: The client's indicative target date for project commencement (Notice to Proceed / NTP) as stated in the RFP. Used for resource mobilisation planning and schedule baseline development in Oracle Primavera P6.
attributes.references: Oracle Primavera P6; FIDIC Procurement Guidelines

attributes.name: bid_bond_percentage
attributes.description: The bid bond (tender guarantee) value expressed as a percentage of the estimated contract value, as required by the client in the RFP. Typically ranges from 1% to 5% of contract value. Null if bid bond is not required.

attributes.name: bid_bond_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the client requires a bid bond (tender guarantee) to be submitted with the proposal (True) or not (False). Bid bonds protect the client against bidder withdrawal after award.

attributes.name: bid_validity_days
attributes.description: The number of calendar days from the submission deadline during which the bidder's proposal must remain valid and binding, as specified in the RFP. Typically 60 to 180 days. Impacts financial exposure and resource commitment.

attributes.name: bim_level
attributes.description: The BIM maturity level required by the client in the RFP: level_1 (CAD-based), level_2 (collaborative BIM with federated models), or level_3 (fully integrated open BIM). Null if BIM is not required.

attributes.name: bim_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the client mandates the use of BIM (Building Information Modeling) for design and construction delivery as specified in the RFP (True) or not (False). Impacts technology requirements and Autodesk BIM 360 platform usage.

attributes.name: client_sector
attributes.description: Classification of the client/owner by sector: public (government/public authority), private (private developer/corporation), ppp (Public-Private Partnership arrangement), or jv (Joint Venture client entity). Drives compliance, reporting, and bid strategy.
attributes.references: FIDIC Procurement Guidelines; IFRS/GAAP; Internal Client Domain

attributes.name: commercial_score_weight
attributes.description: The percentage weighting assigned to the commercial/price component of the bid evaluation, as specified in the RFP (e.g., 40.00 for 40%). Combined with technical_score_weight to total 100%. Null for quality-only evaluations.

attributes.name: contract_type
attributes.description: The pricing and risk-sharing mechanism for the contract as specified in the RFP: lump_sum (fixed price), unit_rate (BOQ-based), cost_plus (reimbursable), target_cost (incentivised), or framework (call-off arrangement). Directly influences bid strategy and cost estimation.

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code for the country where the project is located (e.g., USA, GBR, AUS). Used for regulatory compliance, currency, and jurisdictional reporting.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the contract value and financial terms stated in the RFP (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR, AUD). Required for multi-currency financial reporting and IFRS/GAAP compliance.

attributes.name: defects_liability_period_days
attributes.description: The duration of the Defects Liability Period (DLP) in calendar days as specified in the RFP, commencing from the date of practical completion. Typically 365 or 730 days. Impacts warranty provisioning and post-completion resource planning.

attributes.name: delivery_model
attributes.description: The contractual delivery model specified in the RFP: DBB (Design-Bid-Build), DB (Design-Build), EPC (Engineering Procurement and Construction), GMP (Guaranteed Maximum Price), PPP (Public-Private Partnership), BOT (Build-Operate-Transfer), EPCM (Engineering Procurement Construction Management), or CM (Construction Management). Determines risk allocation and bid structure. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DBB|DB|EPC|GMP|PPP|BOT|EPCM|CM — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: estimated_contract_value
attributes.description: Client's published or internally estimated value of the contract in the nominated currency. Used for bid/no-bid decision-making, bonding requirements, and pipeline forecasting. May be client-disclosed or internally estimated.
attributes.references: IFRS 15; FIDIC Procurement Guidelines; Salesforce CRM Pipeline Forecasting

attributes.name: evaluation_criteria
attributes.description: The overall evaluation methodology specified in the RFP for assessing and ranking bids: price_only (lowest price wins), price_quality (weighted price and technical), quality_only (technical merit), best_value (whole-life cost), or pass_fail (compliance-based). Drives bid strategy.

attributes.name: issue_date
attributes.description: The date on which the RFP/RFQ/ITT was formally issued and released to prospective bidders by the client. Represents the principal business event date for this solicitation record.
attributes.references: FIDIC Procurement Guidelines; Aconex Document Management

attributes.name: issued_timestamp
attributes.description: The system timestamp when this RFP issuance record was first created in the data platform. Represents the audit creation time, distinct from the business issue_date. Used for data lineage and audit trail.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5; ISO 9001; Internal Data Governance

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The system timestamp of the most recent modification to this RFP issuance record. Used for change tracking, data synchronisation, and audit trail compliance.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5; ISO 9001; Internal Data Governance

attributes.name: latest_addendum_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent addendum issued by the client against this RFP. Null if no addenda have been issued. Used to ensure bidders are working from the latest version of the solicitation document.
attributes.references: Aconex Document Management; FIDIC Procurement Guidelines

attributes.name: leed_certification_level
attributes.description: The minimum LEED certification level required by the client as stated in the RFP: certified, silver, gold, or platinum. Null if LEED certification is not required.

attributes.name: leed_certification_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the client has specified a LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) certification requirement for the project in the RFP (True) or not (False). Impacts design, materials, and cost estimation.

attributes.name: liquidated_damages_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether the RFP specifies that Liquidated Damages (LD) will apply for delays or non-performance (True) or not (False). LD clauses are a key risk factor in bid pricing and schedule planning.

attributes.name: liquidated_damages_rate
attributes.description: The daily Liquidated Damages (LD) rate specified in the RFP, expressed in the contract currency. Applied for each calendar day of delay beyond the contractual completion date. Null if LD is not applicable.

attributes.name: local_content_requirement_pct
attributes.description: Minimum percentage of local workforce, materials, or subcontractors required by the client as specified in the RFP. Common in public-sector and government-funded projects. Impacts procurement and subcontractor strategy.
attributes.references: FIDIC Procurement Guidelines; EPA; Internal Procurement Policy

attributes.name: performance_bond_percentage
attributes.description: The performance bond value expressed as a percentage of the contract value, as specified in the RFP. Typically ranges from 5% to 10% of contract value. Null if performance bond is not required.

attributes.name: performance_bond_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the client requires a performance bond to be provided upon contract award (True) or not (False). Performance bonds guarantee the contractor will fulfil contractual obligations.

attributes.name: pre_bid_meeting_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date and time of the mandatory or optional pre-bid conference/site visit where the client clarifies scope and answers bidder questions. Attendance may be a prerequisite for bid eligibility.
attributes.references: FIDIC Procurement Guidelines; Procore Construction Management

attributes.name: pre_bid_meeting_mandatory
attributes.description: Indicates whether attendance at the pre-bid meeting is mandatory for bid eligibility (True) or optional (False). Mandatory attendance is a common client requirement for complex infrastructure projects.

attributes.name: project_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the project scope, works, and deliverables as outlined in the RFP. Includes key scope elements such as civil works, MEP systems, infrastructure type, and geographic extent.

attributes.name: project_location
attributes.description: Geographic location or address of the proposed project site as stated in the RFP. Used for site visit planning, logistics assessment, and regional market analysis.

attributes.name: project_sector
attributes.description: The industry sector classification of the project as described in the RFP. Used for market segmentation, capability matching, and portfolio analytics. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: infrastructure|energy|commercial|residential|industrial|transport|water|healthcare|education|defence — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: project_title
attributes.description: The official name or title of the project as stated in the RFP document. Provides the primary human-readable description of the work being solicited (e.g., 'Highway 45 Expansion Phase 2', 'Airport Terminal C Construction').
attributes.references: FIDIC Procurement Guidelines; Procore Construction Management

attributes.name: rfp_document_reference
attributes.description: The document control reference number or URL/path to the official RFP package in the document management system (Aconex or Autodesk BIM 360). Enables direct retrieval of the source solicitation document.

attributes.name: rfp_number
attributes.description: Externally-known reference number assigned by the client to uniquely identify this solicitation document (RFP, RFQ, or ITT). Used in all correspondence and bid submissions. Sourced from Salesforce CRM Bid Management or Aconex Document Management.

attributes.name: rfp_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the RFP issuance: draft (being prepared), issued (released to market), amended (addendum issued), closed (submission deadline passed), cancelled (withdrawn by client), or awarded (contract awarded). Drives workflow and reporting.
attributes.references: FIDIC Procurement Guidelines; Procore Change Orders

attributes.name: solicitation_type
attributes.description: Classification of the solicitation document type: RFP (Request for Proposal), RFQ (Request for Quotation), ITT (Invitation to Tender), EOI (Expression of Interest), or RFI (Request for Information). Determines the formality and evaluation process applied.

attributes.name: submission_deadline
attributes.description: The exact date and time by which all bid/proposal submissions must be received by the client. Late submissions are typically disqualified. Critical for bid planning and scheduling in Oracle Primavera P6.
attributes.references: FIDIC Procurement Guidelines; Oracle Primavera P6

attributes.name: technical_score_weight
attributes.description: The percentage weighting assigned to the technical/quality component of the bid evaluation, as specified in the RFP (e.g., 60.00 for 60%). Combined with commercial_score_weight to total 100%. Null for price-only evaluations.

products.name: account_credit_profile
products.description: Financial creditworthiness and payment behavior profile for each client account, supporting contract terms negotiation and financial risk management. Captures credit limit, approved payment terms (net 30/60/90), average payment days (DSO), overdue balance, external credit rating (D&B, S&P), internal credit score, last credit review date, payment history rating, credit hold status, special payment arrangements (retention release schedules, milestone-based payments), and sovereign risk indicator for government clients. Updated periodically by finance with input from BD for relationship context.

attributes.name: account_credit_profile_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the account credit profile record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: client_account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the client account for which this credit profile applies. Links to the master client account entity in the client domain.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Customer Master; Salesforce CRM Account Object

attributes.name: approved_payment_terms
attributes.description: Contractually approved payment terms for this client account, governing the number of days within which invoices must be settled or the basis on which payments are triggered. Milestone-based and retention-release terms are common in EPC and FIDIC contracts. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: net_30|net_45|net_60|net_90|milestone_based|retention_release|advance_payment|progress_claim — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FIDIC Conditions of Contract; SAP S/4HANA Payment Terms (FI-AP/AR); IFRS 15 Revenue Recognition

attributes.name: bd_relationship_context
attributes.description: Business Development (BD) team's qualitative assessment of the strategic importance and relationship health of this client account, used as input to the internal credit scoring process. Strategic key accounts may receive more favourable credit terms.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Account Management; Internal Credit Policy

attributes.name: client_segment
attributes.description: Business segment classification of the client account for credit risk segmentation and portfolio analysis. Supports differentiated credit policies for Public-Private Partnership (PPP), Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT), Joint Venture (JV), and private developer clients. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: public_sector|private_sector|ppp|bot|jv_partner|developer|utility|epc_owner|multilateral — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Account Segmentation; Internal Credit Policy; FIDIC

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this credit profile record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail and data lineage in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity and Accountability)

attributes.name: credit_approved_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current credit limit and payment terms were formally approved by the authorised finance approver.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR); Internal Credit Policy; SOX Internal Controls

attributes.name: credit_hold_date
attributes.description: Date on which the credit hold was applied to this client account. Null if no credit hold is currently active.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR); Internal Credit Policy

attributes.name: credit_hold_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this client account is currently placed on credit hold, blocking the issuance of new contracts, purchase orders, or progress claims until the hold is resolved. True = credit hold active; False = normal trading.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR); Internal Credit Policy

attributes.name: credit_hold_reason
attributes.description: Reason code explaining why the credit hold was applied to this client account. Populated only when credit_hold_flag is True. Supports root-cause analysis and escalation workflows.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR); Internal Credit Policy

attributes.name: credit_insurance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether trade credit insurance has been obtained to cover the financial exposure to this client account. True = credit insurance in place; False = no credit insurance.
attributes.references: Internal Credit Policy; IFRS 9; Euler Hermes / Coface Trade Credit Insurance

attributes.name: credit_insurance_limit_amount
attributes.description: Maximum insured amount covered by the trade credit insurance policy for this client account. Populated only when credit_insurance_flag is True.
attributes.references: Internal Credit Policy; IFRS 9; Euler Hermes / Coface Trade Credit Insurance

attributes.name: credit_insurance_provider
attributes.description: Name of the trade credit insurance provider covering the exposure to this client account (e.g., Euler Hermes, Coface, Atradius). Populated only when credit_insurance_flag is True.

attributes.name: credit_limit_amount
attributes.description: Maximum approved credit exposure the business is willing to extend to this client account at any point in time, expressed in the profile currency. Used in contract terms negotiation and financial risk management.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR); IFRS 9; GAAP ASC 310

attributes.name: credit_limit_change_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation of the reason for the most recent change to the credit limit, such as improved payment history, new contract award, rating upgrade, or financial distress. Supports audit trail and governance requirements.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR); Internal Audit; SOX Internal Controls

attributes.name: credit_review_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which this client account's credit profile is formally reviewed. 'triggered' indicates review is event-driven (e.g., new contract award, overdue threshold breach) rather than calendar-based.
attributes.references: Internal Credit Policy; SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR)

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the credit limit, overdue balance, and all monetary fields on this profile are denominated (e.g., USD, GBP, AED, AUD).
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IFRS/GAAP Financial Reporting Standards

attributes.name: current_exposure_amount
attributes.description: Total current financial exposure to this client account, comprising all open invoices (billed but unpaid), unbilled certified work, and retention receivables. Used to assess utilisation against the approved credit limit.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR); IFRS 9; GAAP ASC 310

attributes.name: dso_days
attributes.description: Average number of days this client account takes to pay invoices, calculated over the trailing review period. DSO (Days Sales Outstanding) is a key accounts receivable metric used to assess payment behaviour and cash flow risk. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA AR aging analysis.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Accounts Receivable (FI-AR); IFRS 9; GAAP ASC 310; Viewpoint Vista Job Costing

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which the current credit profile terms (credit limit, payment terms, rating) became effective. Supports temporal tracking of credit profile changes over time.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR); IFRS 9; Internal Credit Policy

attributes.name: effective_until_date
attributes.description: Date until which the current credit profile terms are valid. Null for open-ended profiles. Triggers a review workflow when the current date approaches this date.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR); IFRS 9; Internal Credit Policy

attributes.name: external_credit_rating
attributes.description: Credit rating assigned to the client by an external credit rating agency such as Dun & Bradstreet (D&B), Standard & Poor's (S&P), Moody's, or Fitch. Examples: AAA, AA+, BBB-, Ba1, 5A1 (D&B PAYDEX). Null if no external rating is available.
attributes.references: Dun & Bradstreet (D&B) Credit Rating; S&P Global Ratings; Moody's; IFRS 9

attributes.name: external_rating_agency
attributes.description: Name of the external credit rating agency that issued the external_credit_rating for this client account. Enables multi-agency comparison and source traceability.
attributes.references: Dun & Bradstreet; S&P Global; Moody's; Fitch Ratings; IFRS 9

attributes.name: external_rating_date
attributes.description: Date on which the external credit rating was issued or last confirmed by the rating agency. Used to assess the currency and relevance of the external rating.
attributes.references: Dun & Bradstreet; S&P Global Ratings; IFRS 9

attributes.name: internal_credit_score
attributes.description: Internally calculated credit score assigned to this client account by the finance team, typically on a scale of 0–100 or 0–1000, reflecting payment history, financial strength, project delivery track record, and relationship context provided by Business Development (BD). Higher scores indicate lower credit risk.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR); Internal Credit Policy; IFRS 9

attributes.name: last_credit_review_date
attributes.description: Date on which the most recent formal credit review was completed by the finance team. Triggers periodic reassessment workflows and ensures credit profiles remain current.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR); IFRS 9; Internal Credit Policy

attributes.name: liquidated_damages_exposure_amount
attributes.description: Maximum financial exposure to Liquidated Damages (LD) that the client could apply against the business under active contracts, based on contractual LD rates and project delay risk. Informs credit risk and P&L exposure assessments.
attributes.references: FIDIC Conditions of Contract Clause 8.7; SAP S/4HANA Project Systems; IFRS 15

attributes.name: next_credit_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next periodic credit review of this client account. Supports proactive credit management and ensures timely reassessment before contract renewals or new bid submissions.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR); Internal Credit Policy

attributes.name: overdue_balance_amount
attributes.description: Total outstanding invoice balance that has exceeded the approved payment terms due date as of the last credit review or system refresh. A key indicator for credit hold decisions and risk escalation.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Accounts Receivable (FI-AR); IFRS 9 Expected Credit Loss; GAAP ASC 310

attributes.name: payment_history_rating
attributes.description: Qualitative rating of the client's historical payment behaviour based on analysis of invoice settlement patterns, frequency of late payments, and dispute history. Derived from AR aging data in SAP S/4HANA and Viewpoint Vista.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Accounts Receivable (FI-AR); Viewpoint Vista Job Costing; IFRS 9

attributes.name: payment_terms_days
attributes.description: Numeric representation of the approved payment terms expressed as the number of calendar days from invoice date to due date (e.g., 30 for net-30, 60 for net-60). Complements the approved_payment_terms field for precise DSO calculation and aging analysis.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Payment Terms Configuration; IFRS 15

attributes.name: previous_credit_limit_amount
attributes.description: Credit limit that was in effect prior to the most recent credit review. Enables trend analysis and audit trail of credit limit changes over time.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR); IFRS 9; Internal Audit

attributes.name: profile_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference code assigned to this credit profile, used in correspondence with finance teams and credit agencies. Format: CP- followed by 6-12 alphanumeric characters.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR); Internal Finance Numbering Standard

attributes.name: profile_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the credit profile. 'active' indicates normal trading terms apply; 'credit_hold' indicates all new work or invoicing is blocked pending resolution of overdue balances or risk concerns; 'under_review' indicates a periodic or triggered reassessment is in progress.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR); IFRS 9 Expected Credit Loss

attributes.name: retention_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of each progress claim withheld by the client as retention money under the contract, typically released upon practical completion and expiry of the Defects Liability Period (DLP). Standard construction retention rates range from 5% to 10%.
attributes.references: FIDIC Conditions of Contract Clause 14.3; SAP S/4HANA Project Systems; IFRS 15

attributes.name: retention_release_terms
attributes.description: Terms governing when withheld retention money is released by the client. Common construction arrangements include 50% on practical completion and 50% on Defects Liability Period (DLP) expiry, or full release on a specific milestone.
attributes.references: FIDIC Conditions of Contract Clause 14.9; SAP S/4HANA Project Systems; IFRS 15

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this credit profile data was sourced or last updated. Supports data lineage and reconciliation in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management (FI-AR-CR); Salesforce CRM; Viewpoint Vista; Internal Data Governance

attributes.name: sovereign_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the sovereign government entity when sovereign_risk_flag is True. Used for country-level risk aggregation and geopolitical exposure reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; IFRS 9; World Bank Sovereign Risk Framework

attributes.name: sovereign_risk_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this client account is a government entity or state-owned enterprise subject to sovereign risk considerations, including political risk, currency controls, and delayed payment due to public procurement cycles. True = sovereign/government client; False = private sector client.
attributes.references: FIDIC Conditions of Contract; IFRS 9; World Bank Sovereign Risk Framework; Internal Credit Policy

attributes.name: special_payment_arrangement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a special payment arrangement has been agreed with this client account, such as a retention release schedule, milestone-based payment plan, advance payment structure, or deferred payment agreement. True = special arrangement in place; False = standard terms apply.
attributes.references: FIDIC Conditions of Contract Clause 14; SAP S/4HANA Payment Terms; Internal Credit Policy

attributes.name: special_payment_arrangement_notes
attributes.description: Free-text description of the specific terms of the special payment arrangement, including key milestones, retention percentages, release conditions, or deferred payment schedules agreed with the client.
attributes.references: FIDIC Conditions of Contract; Internal Credit Policy; IFRS 15

attributes.name: special_payment_arrangement_type
attributes.description: Type of special payment arrangement in place for this client account. Populated only when special_payment_arrangement_flag is True. Retention release schedules and milestone-based payments are standard in FIDIC and EPC contracts.
attributes.references: FIDIC Conditions of Contract Clause 14; SAP S/4HANA Payment Terms; IFRS 15

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this credit profile record was last modified in the data platform. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and incremental data processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity and Accountability)

products.name: framework_agreement
products.description: Long-term framework agreements, master service agreements (MSA), or term contracts established with repeat clients, defining pre-agreed rates, scope categories, KPIs, and call-off procedures for multiple projects over a defined period. Captures agreement title, client account, agreement type (framework, MSA, term contract, blanket order), effective date, expiry date, total ceiling value, call-off mechanism, performance KPIs, renewal terms, and extension options. Common with public-sector clients (e.g., highways agencies, utilities) who procure repeat works under a single competitive framework.

attributes.name: framework_agreement_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the framework agreement record in the lakehouse silver layer. Primary key.

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the client account (project owner, developer, or public-sector body) that is party to this framework agreement. Links to the client master product.

attributes.name: client_opportunity_id
attributes.description: Reference to the originating opportunity record in Salesforce CRM from which this framework agreement was won. Enables traceability from bid pipeline to executed agreement for win-rate and revenue analytics.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Opportunity Tracking; Bid Management

attributes.name: contact_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to client.contact. Business justification: client_framework_agreement has a denormalized client_contact_name STRING field representing the primary client contact for the agreement. Normalizing this to a FK contact_id → contact.contact_id repla

attributes.name: parent_agreement_client_framework_agreement_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing identifier linking a call-off contract or lot-level agreement to its parent framework agreement. Supports hierarchical agreement structures where individual call-offs are children of a master framework.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Outline Agreement Hierarchy; FIDIC

attributes.name: agreement_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique reference number assigned to the framework agreement, used in correspondence, call-off orders, and contract administration. Typically issued by the client or procurement authority (e.g., FA-2024-HWY-001).
attributes.references: FIDIC General Conditions; SAP S/4HANA Contract Management

attributes.name: agreement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the long-term agreement structure. 'framework' = competitive framework with multiple call-offs; 'master_service_agreement' (MSA) = pre-agreed terms for repeat services; 'term_contract' = fixed-duration works contract; 'blanket_order' = open purchase order for repeat supply; 'call_off_contract' = individual release under a parent framework.
attributes.references: FIDIC; NEC4 Contract Suite; SAP S/4HANA Outline Agreements

attributes.name: ceiling_value
attributes.description: Maximum total monetary value of all call-off orders that may be placed under this framework agreement over its full term. Acts as the Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) envelope for the framework. Expressed in the agreement currency.
attributes.references: FIDIC General Conditions; IFRS 15 Revenue Recognition; GAAP

attributes.name: client_framework_agreement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the framework agreement. 'draft' = being negotiated; 'active' = in force and accepting call-offs; 'suspended' = temporarily halted; 'expired' = past expiry date with no renewal; 'terminated' = ended early; 'under_renewal' = renewal process initiated.
attributes.references: FIDIC General Conditions Clause 15; SAP S/4HANA Contract Lifecycle

attributes.name: committed_value
attributes.description: Total value of all call-off orders formally issued against this framework agreement to date. Used to track utilisation against the ceiling value and support financial forecasting.
attributes.references: IFRS 15; SAP S/4HANA Project Systems; Viewpoint Vista Job Costing

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the primary jurisdiction in which the framework agreement is executed and governed (e.g., GBR, USA, ARE).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the framework agreement record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Record Control; GDPR Article 5; SAP S/4HANA Audit Log

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the ceiling value, call-off values, and rates are denominated (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR, AED).
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IFRS/GAAP Financial Reporting

attributes.name: delivery_model
attributes.description: Contractual delivery model governing how works are executed under the framework. EPC = Engineering Procurement and Construction; DB = Design-Build; DBB = Design-Bid-Build; PPP = Public-Private Partnership; BOT = Build-Operate-Transfer; MSA = Master Service Agreement; term_maintenance = ongoing maintenance term. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EPC|DB|DBB|PPP|BOT|MSA|term_maintenance — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FIDIC; World Bank Procurement Framework; IBC

attributes.name: dispute_resolution_mechanism

products.name: jv_participant
products.description: This association product represents the Participation role between account and jv_structure. It captures each client entity's formal membership in a Joint Venture arrangement, including their equity stake, committed capital, governance role, and tenure dates. Each record links one account to one jv_structure with attributes that exist only in the context of that specific participation — data that cannot reside on either the account or the JV structure alone.. Existence Justification: In construction, Joint Ventures are co-ownership vehicles where multiple client entities (accounts) simultaneously participate as equity partners in a single JV structure. A single account (e.g., a large infrastructure developer) can participate in multiple JV structures across different projects, and a single JV structure by definition has multiple participating accounts. The current model only captures the lead sponsor via primary_jv_account_id on jv_structure, leaving all non-lead participants entirely unmodelled — a fundamental gap in the business model.

domains.name: contract
domains.description: Authoritative contract repository governing all contractual agreements including FIDIC-based EPC, GMP (Guaranteed Maximum Price), lump-sum, and unit-rate contracts. products.name: agreement
products.description: Master contract record representing the authoritative SSOT for all contractual agreements in the construction domain. Captures FIDIC-based EPC, GMP (Guaranteed Maximum Price), lump-sum, unit-rate, DB (Design-Build), DBB (Design-Bid-Build), PPP (Public-Private Partnership), and BOT (Build-Operate-Transfer) contract types via a type classification attribute. Stores contract identity, scope narrative, detailed scope of works including WBS (Work Breakdown Structure) reference, deliverable descriptions, technical specifications reference, BOQ (Bill of Quantities) linkage, geographic boundaries, and exclusions. Records execution dates, NTP (Notice to Proceed) date, contract value, currency, governing law, dispute resolution mechanism, contract status lifecycle from award through close-out, and particular/special conditions that modify standard form terms. Maintains status transition history for audit and lifecycle analytics. Records all formal amendments including supplemental agreements, deed of variations, and novation agreements with amendment number, type, effective date, revised contract value, revised completion date, and execution status. Serves as the authoritative scope baseline against which change orders and EOT claims are evaluated.

Covers NTP (Notice to Proceed), sectional completion dates, practical completion, DLP start/end dates, performance certificate issuance, and final certificate dates. products.name: payment_schedule
products.description: Defines the contractual payment schedule governing when and how much the employer is obligated to pay the contractor, including full advance payment (mobilization payment) lifecycle management. Captures payment terms, payment intervals, payment due dates, payment method, currency, and supports both milestone-based and time-based payment structures as defined under FIDIC and GMP contract forms. Manages the complete advance payment lifecycle: advance payment amount, percentage of contract value, disbursement date, repayment/recovery schedule, cumulative amount recovered through payment certificate deductions, outstanding advance balance, advance payment guarantee reference, and advance payment status from initial disbursement through full recovery. Serves as the authoritative SSOT for all payment scheduling and advance payment tracking, alongside progress payment and retention release scheduling.

products.name: payment_certificate
products.description: Transactional record of each interim payment certificate (IPC) and final payment certificate (FPC) issued under a main contract or subcontract. Captures certified amount, retention deducted, advance payment recovery, LD deductions, net amount due, certification date, certifier identity, payment due date, and actual payment date. Supports both main contract certification (FIDIC Clause 14) and subcontract payment certification via a contract-level discriminator distinguishing main contract from subcontract certificates. Records subcontract payment applications, certified amounts, and enables back-to-back payment flow management between main contract receipts and subcontractor disbursements. Supports cash flow forecasting, pay-when-paid clause administration, and unified payment reconciliation across the full contract hierarchy.
