products.name: maintenance_order
products.description: Transactional work order record for a specific maintenance activity executed on an asset, generated from a maintenance plan (preventive) or raised as a corrective/breakdown order from a notification. Captures order type (preventive, corrective, breakdown, statutory inspection), priority, planned and actual start/end dates, assigned technician, labor hours, parts consumed (part number, quantity, unit cost per line item), total maintenance cost (labor + parts + external services), order status (created, released, in-progress, completed, technically complete, closed), and SAP PM order number. Supports maintenance cost tracking at labor and parts level, asset downtime analysis, warranty claim evidence, and compliance audit trails. Parts consumption data here serves as the equipment domain's record of materials used — material domain owns stock levels and replenishment.

products.name: inspection_record
products.description: Transactional record of a statutory, regulatory, or internal safety inspection performed on a piece of equipment, and the master register of all resulting compliance certificates issued. Captures inspection type (pre-start check, periodic statutory inspection, OSHA compliance check, crane load test, lifting gear inspection, pressure vessel test, FAT/SAT), inspection date, inspector name and certification, pass/fail outcome, defects identified, corrective actions required, next inspection due date. For certificates: captures certificate type (crane load test certificate, pressure vessel certificate, lifting gear certificate, OSHA compliance certificate, insurance certificate), certificate number, issuing authority, issue date, expiry date, and document storage reference. SSOT for all equipment inspection events AND asset-level compliance certificates. Supports OSHA compliance, insurance requirements, equipment fitness-for-use certification, pre-mobilization compliance checks, and regulatory audit trails. Distinct from quality ITP inspections (owned by quality domain) and operator certifications (which track people, not assets).

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the fuel quantity issued. Common units include litres, gallons, or kWh for electric charging.

products.name: operator_certification
products.description: Master record of an equipment operator's certification, licence, or competency qualification for a specific equipment type or class. Captures operator reference (linked to workforce domain), equipment category certified for (e.g., tower crane, mobile crane, excavator, forklift), certifying body, certificate number, issue date, expiry date, certification status (valid, expired, suspended), and renewal requirements. Supports OSHA compliance, HSE pre-start checks, and operator-to-equipment assignment validation. Owned by equipment domain as it governs equipment operation rights.
products.reference: OSHA Operator Certification / Crane Operator Licence

attributes.name: operator_certification_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the operator certification record. Primary key for the operator certification entity.

attributes.name: asset_category_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to equipment.asset_category. Business justification: Operator certification is tied to an equipment category; replace free‑text category with FK to asset_category to enforce consistency.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Certification costs are charged to cost centers for departmental training cost allocation and overhead reporting. Construction finance teams require cost center on certification records to allocate wo

attributes.name: cost_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_code. Business justification: Operator certification costs (cost_amount field) are allocated to cost codes for construction workforce cost tracking and training budget reporting. Cost controllers classify certification spend by co

attributes.name: craft_worker_id
attributes.description: Reference to the equipment operator in the workforce domain who holds this certification. Links to the workforce master data to identify the individual operator.

attributes.name: document_register_id
attributes.description: Reference to the digital document or scanned copy of the physical certification document stored in the document management system. Links to Aconex or BIM 360 document repository.

attributes.name: regulatory_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_obligation. Business justification: Operator certifications (crane operator licenses, forklift certifications) are mandated by specific regulatory obligations (OSHA 1926, state licensing boards). Linking operator_certification to the go

attributes.name: tender_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to bid.tender. Business justification: Tender prequalification compliance: clients require proof of certified operators for specialized plant (cranes, piling rigs) as part of tender submission. Linking certifications to the tender supports

attributes.name: training_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.training. Business justification: Operator certifications are issued as outcomes of safety training events. The training_id on operator_certification links the certification to the specific training record that produced it, supporting

attributes.name: assessment_date
attributes.description: The date on which the operator completed the certification assessment or examination. Represents the formal evaluation event.

attributes.name: assessor_name
attributes.description: Name of the qualified assessor or examiner who conducted the certification assessment and validated the operators competency.

attributes.name: capacity_rating
attributes.description: The maximum capacity or tonnage rating of equipment the operator is certified to operate, such as cranes up to 100 tons or forklifts up to 5 tons. Defines operational limits for equipment assignment.

attributes.name: certificate_number
attributes.description: Unique certificate or license number issued by the certifying body. This is the externally-known identifier for the certification document.

attributes.name: certification_level
attributes.description: The proficiency or skill level represented by the certification, such as basic, intermediate, advanced, or master operator. Indicates the complexity of equipment and operations the operator is qualified to perform. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: basic|intermediate|advanced|master|trainee|journeyman|supervisor — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: certification_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the certification. Indicates whether the certification is valid and active, expired, suspended, revoked, or pending renewal. Critical for HSE pre-start checks and operator assignment validation.

attributes.name: certification_type
attributes.description: The type or nature of the certification, such as operator license, competency card, safety certification, or manufacturer-specific certification.

attributes.name: certifying_body
attributes.description: Name of the organization, authority, or institution that issued the certification. Examples include NCCCO, OSHA-approved training providers, manufacturer training centers, or government licensing authorities.

attributes.name: certifying_body_accreditation_number
attributes.description: Accreditation or registration number of the certifying body, validating that the issuing organization is authorized to provide certifications.

attributes.name: cost_amount
attributes.description: The total cost incurred to obtain or renew this certification, including training fees, examination fees, and administrative charges. Used for workforce development cost tracking.

attributes.name: cost_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the certification cost amount. Enables multi-currency cost tracking for international operations.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this certification record was first created in the system. Follows ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: endorsements
attributes.description: Additional endorsements, specializations, or restrictions associated with the certification, such as night operations, confined spaces, or specific attachment types. Comma-separated list of endorsement codes or descriptions.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which the certification expires and is no longer valid. Operators must renew or recertify before this date to maintain valid certification status.

attributes.name: issue_date
attributes.description: The date on which the certification was originally issued to the operator. Represents the start of the certification validity period.

attributes.name: issuing_country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the country in which the certification was issued. Important for cross-border projects and international operator mobility.

attributes.name: issuing_state_province
attributes.description: State, province, or regional jurisdiction within the issuing country where the certification was granted. Relevant for jurisdictions with state-level licensing requirements.

attributes.name: last_renewal_date
attributes.description: The most recent date on which the certification was renewed or recertified. Tracks the certification maintenance history.

attributes.name: medical_clearance_date
attributes.description: The date on which the operator received medical clearance or passed the required health examination for this certification. Nullable if medical clearance is not required.

attributes.name: medical_clearance_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which the medical clearance expires and must be renewed. Nullable if medical clearance is not required or does not expire.

attributes.name: medical_clearance_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a medical examination or health clearance is required as part of the certification or renewal process. True if medical clearance is mandatory, false otherwise.

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: User identifier or name of the person who last modified this certification record. Provides audit trail for data changes.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this certification record was last modified in the system. Follows ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: next_renewal_due_date
attributes.description: The date by which the operator must complete renewal requirements to maintain continuous certification. Used for proactive renewal planning and compliance tracking.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, comments, or special conditions related to the certification. Captures contextual information not covered by structured fields.

attributes.name: practical_assessment_score
attributes.description: Score or grade achieved by the operator in the practical hands-on assessment component of the certification. Typically expressed as a percentage or numeric score.

attributes.name: reciprocity_agreements
attributes.description: List of countries, states, or jurisdictions where this certification is recognized under reciprocity or mutual recognition agreements. Enables cross-jurisdictional operator deployment.
attributes.references: FIDIC International Federation of Consulting Engineers

attributes.name: renewal_requirement
attributes.description: Description of the requirements the operator must fulfill to renew the certification, such as refresher training hours, re-assessment, continuing education credits, or medical examination.

attributes.name: restrictions
attributes.description: Any limitations or restrictions placed on the certification, such as daylight operations only, supervised operation required, or specific site conditions. Defines operational boundaries for the operator.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the operational system from which this certification record originated, such as SAP SuccessFactors, Intelex, or HCSS HeavyJob. Enables data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier of this certification record in the source operational system. Enables traceability and reconciliation with source systems.

attributes.name: sponsor_organization
attributes.description: Name of the organization that sponsored or paid for the operators certification training and examination. May be the construction company, a subcontractor, or the operator themselves.

attributes.name: theory_assessment_score
attributes.description: Score or grade achieved by the operator in the theoretical or written examination component of the certification. Typically expressed as a percentage or numeric score.

attributes.name: training_hours_completed
attributes.description: Total number of training hours completed by the operator to achieve this certification. Demonstrates the depth of training and preparation.

attributes.name: verification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the certification was last verified with the certifying body or through an independent verification process.

attributes.name: verification_status
attributes.description: Status of the certification verification process, indicating whether the certification has been independently verified with the issuing body. Critical for compliance and audit purposes.

attributes.name: verified_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the person, system, or organization that performed the certification verification. Provides audit trail for verification activities.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User identifier or name of the person who created this certification record in the system. Provides audit trail for data entry.

domains.name: workforce
domains.description: Construction workforce management domain tracking labor resources, crew assignments, time tracking, production rates, skill certifications, labor cost coding, field personnel deployment, and site access records. Manages craft labor, supervision, and project-based staffing distinct from corporate HR functions. Integrates with HCSS HeavyJob for timesheets and SAP SuccessFactors for HCM.

products.name: craft_worker
products.description: Master record for all craft labor personnel deployed on construction projects including hourly trade workers and working foremen/supervisors. Captures worker identity, trade classification (from skill_trade taxonomy), employment type (direct hire, agency, union referral), union affiliation and local, craft code, supervisory role flag, home project assignment, mobilization status, security clearance level, and field deployment history. SSOT for individual field worker identity in the workforce domain. Workers may hold multiple trade classifications and rotate between craft and supervisory roles across projects. Integrates with SAP SuccessFactors for HCM master data and HCSS HeavyJob for field time tracking.

attributes.name: craft_worker_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the craft worker record. Primary key for the craft worker entity.

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to client.account. Business justification: Payroll & compliance reports require each worker to be linked to the employing client account for tax, insurance and HSE reporting.

attributes.name: construction_project_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the primary construction project to which the craft worker is currently assigned as their home base.

attributes.name: labor_cost_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.labor_cost_code. Business justification: A craft worker is classified under a specific labor cost code that defines their trade, skill level, wage classification, and burden rates. Adding labor_cost_code_id normalizes the craft_code string i

attributes.name: party_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.contract_party. Business justification: REQUIRED: Workers are employed by a contract party (contractor/sub‑contractor); linking supports payroll, insurance, and compliance reporting.

attributes.name: permit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.permit. Business justification: Each permit designates a responsible worker (permit holder) to ensure compliance; linking enables accountability audits.

attributes.name: skill_trade_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.skill_trade. Business justification: Standardize trade information by referencing skill_trade; remove redundant primary_trade_code and primary_trade_name from craft_worker.

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: REQUIRED: Vendor‑Supplied Labor Tracking – each subcontractor worker must be linked to the vendor that supplies them for compliance and cost allocation.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the craft worker record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the worker's compensation (e.g., USD, CAD, GBP).

attributes.name: demobilization_date
attributes.description: Date the craft worker was demobilized from their project assignment, if applicable.

attributes.name: email_address
attributes.description: Primary email address for the craft worker used for communication and system access.

attributes.name: emergency_contact_name

attributes.name: emergency_contact_phone
attributes.description: Phone number of the craft worker's designated emergency contact person.

attributes.name: emergency_contact_relationship
attributes.description: Relationship of the emergency contact to the craft worker (e.g., spouse, parent, sibling, friend).

attributes.name: employment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the worker's employment relationship with the organization: direct hire (permanent employee), agency (temporary staffing), union referral (union hall dispatch), or subcontractor (independent contractor).

attributes.name: first_name
attributes.description: Legal first name of the craft worker as recorded in HR systems.

attributes.name: hire_date
attributes.description: Date the craft worker was hired or first engaged by the organization.

attributes.name: hourly_base_rate
attributes.description: Standard hourly wage rate for the craft worker in their primary trade classification, excluding overtime premiums and benefits.

attributes.name: last_name
attributes.description: Legal last name of the craft worker as recorded in HR systems.

attributes.name: middle_name
attributes.description: Middle name or initial of the craft worker, if applicable.

attributes.name: mobilization_date
attributes.description: Date the craft worker was mobilized to their current project assignment.

attributes.name: mobilization_status
attributes.description: Current deployment status of the craft worker: mobilized (actively deployed to a project site), demobilized (released from project), on_leave (temporarily unavailable), or available (ready for assignment).

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the craft worker record was last modified in the system.

attributes.name: osha_certification_expiry_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Certification Expiry Date
attributes.description: Expiration date of the craft worker's OSHA safety certification, if applicable.

attributes.name: osha_certification_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Certification Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the craft worker holds valid OSHA safety training certification (e.g., OSHA 10-hour or 30-hour).

attributes.name: overtime_rate_multiplier
attributes.description: Multiplier applied to base hourly rate for overtime hours (e.g., 1.5 for time-and-a-half, 2.0 for double-time).

attributes.name: phone_number
attributes.description: Primary contact phone number for the craft worker for emergency contact and field coordination.

attributes.name: ppe_size_boots
attributes.description: Boot size for issuing Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) such as steel-toed safety boots.

attributes.name: ppe_size_pants
attributes.description: Pants size for issuing Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) such as work pants and coveralls.

attributes.name: ppe_size_shirt
attributes.description: Shirt size for issuing Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) such as high-visibility vests and work shirts. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: XS|S|M|L|XL|XXL|XXXL — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: security_clearance_level
attributes.description: Security clearance level held by the craft worker for access to restricted project sites (e.g., government, defense, critical infrastructure projects).

attributes.name: site_access_badge_number
attributes.description: Unique badge or access card number issued to the craft worker for site entry and time tracking at construction sites.

attributes.name: skill_level
attributes.description: Proficiency level of the craft worker in their primary trade: apprentice (in training), journeyman (certified tradesperson), master (advanced certification), or foreman (supervisory level).

attributes.name: supervisory_role_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the craft worker currently holds a supervisory role such as working foreman or crew lead (True) or is a non-supervisory hourly worker (False).

attributes.name: supervisory_title
attributes.description: Job title for supervisory role if applicable (e.g., Working Foreman, Crew Lead, General Foreman).

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Date the craft worker's employment or engagement was terminated, if applicable.

attributes.name: union_affiliation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the craft worker is affiliated with a labor union (True) or non-union (False).

attributes.name: union_local_number

attributes.name: union_name
attributes.description: Name of the labor union the worker is affiliated with, if applicable (e.g., International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, United Association of Plumbers).

attributes.name: worker_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the craft worker record: active (currently employed and available), inactive (temporarily not working), suspended (disciplinary or safety hold), or terminated (employment ended).

attributes.name: years_of_experience
attributes.description: Total number of years of experience the craft worker has in their primary trade.

products.name: crew
products.description: Master record for a named field crew or gang deployed on a construction project. Captures crew name, crew type (civil, MEP, structural, concrete, etc.), foreman assignment, home cost code, project assignment, crew size, and active status. A crew is the primary unit of field labor organization in construction operations. Distinct from individual worker records.

attributes.name: crew_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the construction crew. Primary key for the crew entity.

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to client.account. Business justification: Crew budgeting and resource allocation dashboards aggregate crew costs per client account, needing a direct account FK.

attributes.name: agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.agreement. Business justification: REQUIRED: Crew allocation is planned per contract agreement; linking allows crew costs and productivity to be attributed to the agreement.

attributes.name: construction_project_id
attributes.description: Reference to the construction project to which this crew is currently assigned. A crew may be reassigned between projects over its lifecycle.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Required for crew cost allocation reports that roll crew labor costs to the project's cost center, enabling accurate budgeting and variance analysis per cost center.

attributes.name: cost_code_id
attributes.description: Reference to the home cost code for this crew. Used for labor cost allocation and job costing when crew time is not charged to a specific activity cost code.

attributes.name: craft_worker_id
attributes.description: Reference to the worker record of the foreman or crew lead responsible for supervising this crew. The foreman is accountable for crew productivity, safety, and quality.

attributes.name: hse_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.hse_plan. Business justification: Crews operate under a specific site HSE plan governing their PPE requirements, induction procedures, and emergency response protocols. Linking crew to hse_plan enables crew-level HSE compliance report

attributes.name: labor_cost_code_id

attributes.name: permit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.permit. Business justification: Hot‑work permits assign a specific crew; tracking crew per permit is required for safety compliance reports.

attributes.name: skill_trade_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.skill_trade. Business justification: A crew in construction is typically organized around a primary trade discipline (e.g., ironworker crew, pipefitter crew, concrete crew). Adding skill_trade_id to crew directly classifies the crew's pr

attributes.name: average_hourly_rate
attributes.description: Blended average hourly labor rate for the crew, calculated across all crew members. Used for cost estimation and Earned Value Management (EVM) calculations. Currency is USD unless otherwise specified in project configuration.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this crew record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: crew_code
attributes.description: Business identifier code for the crew used in field operations and timekeeping systems. Typically alphanumeric and unique within a project or division.

attributes.name: crew_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the crew, often reflecting the crew type, foreman name, or project assignment (e.g., 'Smith Concrete Gang', 'MEP Crew A').

attributes.name: crew_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the crew in its lifecycle. Active crews are deployed and working; inactive crews are not currently assigned; mobilizing/demobilizing crews are in transition; standby crews are available but not deployed; disbanded crews are permanently closed.

attributes.name: crew_type
attributes.description: Classification of the crew based on trade or discipline. Defines the primary craft or work scope the crew is organized to perform. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: civil|structural|concrete|mep|electrical|plumbing|hvac|finishing|earthworks|piling — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: days_since_last_incident
attributes.description: Number of calendar days since the last recordable safety incident for this crew. Used for safety milestone recognition and Total Recordable Incident Rate (TRIR) tracking. Null if no incidents have occurred.

attributes.name: demobilization_date
attributes.description: Planned or actual date when the crew will be or was demobilized from the current project. Null for active crews with no planned demobilization.

attributes.name: home_location
attributes.description: Primary site, yard, or facility where this crew is based or reports to. May be a project site, equipment yard, or regional office.

attributes.name: is_union_crew
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this is a union crew subject to collective bargaining agreements and union work rules. True if union, false if non-union or open shop.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this crew record was last updated. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data synchronization across systems.

attributes.name: last_safety_incident_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent recordable safety incident involving this crew. Used for safety performance tracking and Lost Time Injury (LTI) frequency calculations. Null if no incidents have occurred.

attributes.name: mobilization_date
attributes.description: Date when the crew was mobilized and became operational on the current project or assignment. Used for crew lifecycle tracking and project staffing history.

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: User ID or name of the person who last modified this crew record. Used for audit trail and accountability in crew management.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional information about the crew, such as special skills, project-specific arrangements, or operational constraints. Used by project management and field supervision.

attributes.name: planned_crew_size
attributes.description: Target or planned number of workers for this crew based on project staffing plans and Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) resource requirements.

attributes.name: productivity_rate
attributes.description: Standard or historical productivity rate for this crew, expressed in units per hour (e.g., cubic yards of concrete per hour, linear feet of pipe per hour). Unit of measure depends on crew type and work scope.

attributes.name: productivity_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the productivity rate (e.g., CY/HR for cubic yards per hour, LF/HR for linear feet per hour, EA/HR for each per hour). Aligns with Bill of Quantities (BOQ) units.

attributes.name: quality_rating
attributes.description: Current quality performance rating for the crew based on Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC) inspections, Non-Conformance Reports (NCR), and rework rates. Used for crew selection and quality incentive programs.

attributes.name: required_certifications
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of skill certifications or licenses required for crew members (e.g., 'OSHA 30, Confined Space, Rigging Level II'). Used for crew qualification verification and compliance with Inspection and Test Plans (ITP).

attributes.name: safety_rating
attributes.description: Current safety performance rating for the crew based on Health Safety and Environment (HSE) inspections, incident history, and compliance with Safe Work Method Statements (SWMS). Used for crew selection and safety incentive programs.

attributes.name: shift_end_time
attributes.description: Standard end time for the crew's shift in HH:MM format (24-hour clock). Used for timesheet validation and labor hour planning.

attributes.name: shift_start_time
attributes.description: Standard start time for the crew's shift in HH:MM format (24-hour clock). Used for timesheet validation and site access control.

attributes.name: shift_type
attributes.description: Standard shift pattern for this crew. Day shift is typical daytime hours; night shift is overnight; swing shift is evening; rotating shifts alternate; extended shifts are longer than standard 8-hour shifts.

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Current number of workers assigned to this crew, including the foreman. Used for resource planning and productivity rate calculations.

attributes.name: union_affiliation
attributes.description: Name of the labor union or trade association to which the majority of crew members belong, if applicable. Null for non-union crews. Relevant for labor relations, collective bargaining agreements, and jurisdictional work rules.

products.description: Transactional record linking individual craft workers to a specific crew for a defined period on a project. Captures worker role within the crew (laborer, operator, foreman, lead), assignment start and end dates, cost code, WBS element, shift, and assignment status. Enables tracking of crew composition changes over time and supports labor cost allocation.

attributes.name: assignment_notes

attributes.name: assignment_reason

products.name: labor_cost_code
products.description: Unified reference master for labor cost codes and trade/skill classifications used to classify and allocate field labor expenditure and define workforce competency categories. Captures cost code identifier, description, trade code, trade name, craft discipline (ironworker, pipefitter, electrician, carpenter, etc.), union jurisdiction, prevailing wage classification, required certification types, budget category, SAP PS (Project Systems) WBS mapping, and active status. Serves as the single source of truth for both cost allocation and trade/skill classification — the authoritative taxonomy of construction trades and their cost coding. Integrates with SAP S/4HANA Project Systems and HCSS HeavyJob cost coding structures. Referenced by timesheets, labor rates, agency orders, and staffing plans for consistent trade and cost classification.

Business justification: Each skill trade in construction is governed by a specific regulatory obligation (state licensing law, OSHA training mandate, apprenticeship ratio requirement). skill_trade has osha_training_requireme

attributes.name: apprenticeship_duration_hours
attributes.description: Standard duration of apprenticeship training program in hours (e.g., 8000 hours for journeyman electrician). Used for workforce development planning and training program management.

attributes.name: apprenticeship_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether formal apprenticeship training is required or recommended for this trade skill. True if apprenticeship is a standard pathway; false otherwise.

attributes.name: average_hourly_rate_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Average Hourly Rate United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Average or benchmark hourly labor rate for journeyman-level workers in this trade, in US dollars. Used for project cost estimation and budget planning. Actual rates vary by geography, project type, and union agreements.

attributes.name: bim_integration_level
attributes.description: Level of BIM (Building Information Modeling) technology integration and digital literacy expected for this trade (none, basic, intermediate, advanced). Used for technology training planning and digital construction readiness.

attributes.name: certification_issuing_body
attributes.description: Name of the organization or regulatory body that issues the required certification for this trade (e.g., NCCER, AWS, NCCCO, state licensing board). Used for credential verification and compliance tracking.
attributes.references: OSHA, NFPA, ACI, AISC, AWS Standards

attributes.name: certification_type_required
attributes.description: Type of professional certification, license, or credential required to perform work in this trade (e.g., NCCER certification, state electrical license, AWS welding certification, NCCCO crane operator certification). Multiple certifications may be listed as comma-separated values.
attributes.references: OSHA, NFPA, ACI, AISC, AWS Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this trade skill record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this trade skill classification was retired or became obsolete. Null for currently active trades. Used for temporal validity and historical analysis.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this trade skill classification became active and available for use in workforce planning and assignment. Used for temporal validity and historical tracking.

attributes.name: equipment_dependency_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this trade requires specialized heavy equipment or machinery to perform work (e.g., crane operators require cranes, equipment operators require excavators). True if equipment-dependent; false if primarily manual labor.

attributes.name: hazard_exposure_level
attributes.description: Classification of typical occupational hazard exposure level for this trade (low, moderate, high, extreme). Used for risk assessment, insurance rating, and HSE planning.

attributes.name: labor_shortage_indicator
attributes.description: Current market assessment of labor availability for this trade (surplus, balanced, shortage, critical shortage). Used for strategic workforce planning and recruitment prioritization.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this trade skill record was last updated or modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: mep_discipline_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Mechanical Electrical and Plumbing (MEP) Discipline Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this trade is part of the MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing) disciplines. True for electricians, pipefitters, HVAC technicians, plumbers; false for structural and civil trades.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, comments, or special considerations related to this trade skill classification. May include regional variations, specialty sub-disciplines, or unique requirements.

attributes.name: osha_training_requirement
attributes.business_glossary_term: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Training Requirement
attributes.description: Specific OSHA training courses or certifications required for this trade (e.g., OSHA 10-hour, OSHA 30-hour, confined space, fall protection, scaffolding). Used for safety compliance and site access control.

attributes.name: overtime_multiplier
attributes.description: Standard overtime pay multiplier for this trade (e.g., 1.5 for time-and-a-half, 2.0 for double-time). Used for labor cost calculation and payroll processing.
attributes.references: Fair Labor Standards Act, Union Agreements

attributes.name: physical_demand_rating
attributes.description: Classification of physical exertion and strength requirements for this trade (light, medium, heavy, very heavy). Used for workforce health management and ergonomic planning.

attributes.name: ppe_requirements
attributes.description: Standard personal protective equipment required for workers in this trade (e.g., hard hat, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves, fall protection harness, welding helmet). Used for safety planning and PPE procurement.

attributes.name: prevailing_wage_classification
attributes.description: Official wage classification code used for prevailing wage determination on public works projects, as defined by Davis-Bacon Act or state-specific prevailing wage laws. Critical for labor cost estimation and compliance on government-funded projects.

attributes.name: productivity_unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Standard unit of measure used to track productivity for this trade (e.g., linear feet of pipe installed per day, cubic yards of concrete placed per hour, square feet of drywall hung per shift). Used for production tracking and earned value management (EVM).

attributes.name: seasonal_demand_pattern
attributes.description: Description of typical seasonal demand fluctuation for this trade (e.g., high demand in summer for outdoor trades, year-round for indoor MEP work). Used for workforce capacity planning and recruitment timing.

attributes.name: skill_level_tiers
attributes.description: Defined progression tiers or grades within this trade (e.g., apprentice, journeyman, foreman, general foreman, superintendent). Used for career path planning and labor rate determination. Typically stored as comma-separated hierarchy.

attributes.name: standard_crew_size
attributes.description: Typical or recommended crew size for efficient work execution in this trade (e.g., 4-person ironworker crew, 2-person electrician crew). Used for resource planning and scheduling.

attributes.name: trade_category
attributes.description: High-level classification grouping of the trade skill (structural, mechanical, electrical, civil, finishing, equipment operation, specialty). Used for workforce segmentation and reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: structural|mechanical|electrical|civil|finishing|equipment_operation|specialty — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: trade_code
attributes.description: Standardized alphanumeric code identifying the construction trade or craft discipline (e.g., IW for ironworker, EL for electrician, CP for carpenter). Used for workforce planning, labor rate determination, and crew composition.

attributes.name: trade_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the construction trade or craft discipline (e.g., Ironworker, Pipefitter, Electrician, Carpenter, Concrete Finisher, Heavy Equipment Operator, Rigger, Welder).

attributes.name: trade_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the trade skill classification. Active trades are available for workforce planning and assignment; inactive trades are no longer used; obsolete trades are deprecated; emerging trades are newly recognized.

attributes.name: travel_requirement_typical
attributes.description: Typical geographic travel requirement for workers in this trade (none, local, regional, national, international). Used for workforce planning and per diem budgeting.

attributes.name: union_jurisdiction_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the labor union or trade union that has jurisdiction over this craft discipline (e.g., IBEW for electricians, UA for pipefitters, IUOE for operators). Used for labor relations, collective bargaining, and compliance.

attributes.name: union_jurisdiction_name
attributes.description: Full name of the labor union or trade union with jurisdiction over this craft (e.g., International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, United Association of Plumbers and Pipefitters).

Captures mobilization type (initial, transfer, demobilization), origin and destination project, travel arrangement details, per diem entitlement, mobilization date, demobilization date, and associated cost. Supports project staffing planning and labor cost forecasting.

attributes.name: labor_mobilization_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the labor mobilization record. Primary key for tracking worker movement to/from project sites.

attributes.name: activity_id

attributes.name: cash_flow_forecast_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cash_flow_forecast. Business justification: Labor mobilization events (travel, accommodation, per diem) represent significant discrete cash outflows. Construction finance teams link mobilization records to cash flow forecasts to capture mobiliz

attributes.name: checklist_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.checklist. Business justification: Site induction compliance: labor_mobilization tracks hse_orientation_completed_flag and hse_orientation_date driven by a specific site induction checklist. Linking to the checklist record enables audi

attributes.name: contract_milestone_id

Construction schedulers track which milestone authorized ea

attributes.name: destination_construction_project_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the project site the worker is mobilizing to. Null for demobilizations.

attributes.name: primary_labor_construction_project_id

attributes.name: regulatory_obligation_id

attributes.name: site_mobilization_id

attributes.name: accommodation_booking_reference

attributes.name: accommodation_cost_estimate
attributes.description: Estimated total cost of temporary accommodation for the mobilization period.

attributes.name: accommodation_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether temporary accommodation is required at the destination site (True) or not (False).

attributes.name: actual_arrival_timestamp
attributes.description: Actual date and time the worker arrived at the destination project site, recorded for compliance and payroll purposes.

attributes.name: actual_departure_timestamp
attributes.description: Actual date and time the worker departed from the origin project site, recorded for compliance and payroll purposes.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date the mobilization request was formally approved by authorized personnel.

attributes.name: craft_code
attributes.description: Code representing the worker's primary trade or craft skill (e.g., CARP for carpenter, ELEC for electrician, WELD for welder).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the mobilization record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this mobilization record.

attributes.name: demobilization_date
attributes.description: Date the worker is scheduled to depart from the origin project site. Null for initial mobilizations.

attributes.name: hse_orientation_completed_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Safety and Environment (HSE) Orientation Completed Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the worker has completed mandatory HSE (Health Safety and Environment) site orientation at the destination project (True) or not (False).

attributes.name: hse_orientation_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Safety and Environment (HSE) Orientation Date
attributes.description: Date the worker completed HSE (Health Safety and Environment) orientation training at the destination site.
attributes.references: OSHA Occupational Safety and Health Administration

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.name: mobilization_date

attributes.name: mobilization_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the mobilization transaction. Format: MOB-YYYYMMDD followed by sequence number.

attributes.name: mobilization_reason
attributes.description: Business justification or reason for the mobilization (e.g., project ramp-up, skill shortage, emergency response, project closeout).

attributes.name: mobilization_status
attributes.description: Current status of the mobilization transaction in its lifecycle workflow.

attributes.name: mobilization_type
attributes.description: Type of mobilization event: initial (first assignment to project), transfer (move between projects), demobilization (release from project), remobilization (return after temporary leave).

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional free-text notes or comments related to the mobilization transaction for operational reference.

attributes.name: per_diem_duration_days
attributes.description: Number of days the worker is entitled to receive per diem allowance.

attributes.name: per_diem_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the worker is eligible for per diem allowance during mobilization (True) or not (False).

attributes.name: per_diem_rate
attributes.description: Daily per diem allowance rate in the project's currency for meals and incidental expenses.

attributes.name: site_access_badge_issued_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a site access badge or credential has been issued to the worker at the destination site (True) or not (False).

attributes.name: special_requirements
attributes.description: Any special requirements or considerations for the mobilization such as medical accommodations, dietary restrictions, security clearances, or equipment transport needs.

attributes.name: total_mobilization_cost
attributes.description: Total estimated or actual cost of the mobilization including travel, accommodation, per diem, and administrative expenses.

attributes.name: travel_booking_reference
attributes.description: Booking confirmation number or reference code for travel arrangements (flight, train, rental car).

attributes.name: travel_cost_estimate
attributes.description: Estimated total cost of travel arrangements including airfare, ground transportation, and related expenses.

attributes.name: travel_mode
attributes.description: Primary mode of transportation arranged for the worker's mobilization journey.

products.name: staffing_plan
products.description: Master record for a project-level workforce staffing plan defining the planned headcount, trade mix, and labor hours required by project phase, WBS element, and time period. Captures planned vs. actual headcount, peak labor requirements, trade breakdown, source strategy (direct hire, subcontract, agency), ramp-up/ramp-down curves, and plan version. Supports workforce forecasting, labor procurement decisions, and project mobilization planning. Integrates with SAP SuccessFactors workforce planning.

attributes.name: staffing_plan_id
attributes.description: Primary key for staffing_plan

attributes.name: agreement_id

attributes.name: project_engagement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to client.project_engagement. Business justification: Staffing plans are developed in direct response to contract awards captured in project_engagement, which defines NTP dates, headcount obligations, and labor commitments. Construction workforce planner

attributes.name: wbs_element_id
attributes.description: Reference to the WBS element this staffing plan applies to, enabling phase-specific or activity-specific workforce planning.

attributes.name: wbs_node_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to schedule.wbs_node. Business justification: Staffing plans in construction are structured around schedule WBS nodes (work packages/control accounts) for labor resource loading. This link enables earned value management — comparing planned labor

attributes.name: accommodation_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether worker accommodation (camps, hotels, per diem) is required for this staffing plan, typically true for remote or large-scale projects.

attributes.name: actual_headcount
attributes.description: Actual number of workers deployed as of the last reporting period, enabling planned vs. actual variance analysis.

attributes.name: actual_labor_hours
attributes.description: Actual labor hours worked as of the last reporting period, supporting Earned Value Management (EVM) and productivity tracking.

attributes.name: agency_headcount

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which this staffing plan was formally approved and authorized for execution.

attributes.name: approved_by

attributes.name: baseline_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this staffing plan is the approved baseline against which all future revisions and actuals will be compared.

attributes.name: craft_labor_headcount
attributes.description: Number of skilled trade workers (carpenters, electricians, welders, masons, etc.) planned for the period.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this staffing plan record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: direct_hire_headcount
attributes.description: Number of workers planned to be sourced through direct employment by the general contractor or project owner.

attributes.name: headcount_variance
attributes.description: Difference between planned and actual headcount (actual minus planned), indicating over- or under-staffing relative to the plan.

attributes.name: labor_hours_variance
attributes.description: Difference between planned and actual labor hours (actual minus planned), supporting cost and schedule performance analysis.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this staffing plan record was last updated, supporting audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, assumptions, constraints, or special instructions related to this staffing plan.

attributes.name: peak_headcount
attributes.description: Maximum number of workers required at any single point during the planning period, critical for site logistics, accommodation, and safety planning.

attributes.name: peak_headcount_date
attributes.description: Date on which the peak headcount is expected to occur, enabling targeted resource mobilization and site readiness planning.

attributes.name: plan_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the staffing plan indicating its approval state and operational validity.

attributes.name: plan_type
attributes.description: Classification of the staffing plan indicating its purpose (baseline for original plan, forecast for updated projections, scenario for what-if analysis).

attributes.name: plan_version
attributes.description: Version identifier for the staffing plan, enabling tracking of plan revisions and baseline comparisons (e.g., 'V1.0', 'V2.1', 'Baseline', 'Revised').

attributes.name: planning_period_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the time period covered by this staffing plan, defining the conclusion of the workforce deployment window.

attributes.name: planning_period_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the time period covered by this staffing plan, defining the beginning of the workforce deployment window.

attributes.name: ramp_down_end_date
attributes.description: Date when workforce demobilization is complete, marking the end of the labor deployment for this plan.

attributes.name: ramp_down_start_date
attributes.description: Date when workforce demobilization begins, marking the start of the labor reduction curve as project activities wind down.

attributes.name: ramp_up_end_date
attributes.description: Date when workforce reaches full planned strength, marking the end of the mobilization phase.

attributes.name: ramp_up_start_date
attributes.description: Date when workforce mobilization and ramp-up begins, marking the start of the labor deployment curve.

attributes.name: site_access_requirements
attributes.description: Description of site access prerequisites for workers (security clearances, background checks, client-specific badging), critical for mobilization planning.

attributes.name: skill_certification_requirements
attributes.description: Summary of mandatory certifications and qualifications required for workers in this staffing plan (e.g., 'OSHA 30, Confined Space, Rigging Level II'), supporting compliance and safety planning.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifier of the operational system from which this staffing plan record originated (e.g., 'SAP SuccessFactors', 'Oracle Primavera P6', 'Procore').

attributes.name: sourcing_strategy
attributes.description: Primary workforce sourcing approach for this staffing plan, defining how labor will be procured and managed.

attributes.name: subcontractor_headcount
attributes.description: Number of workers planned to be provided by subcontractors under contract to the general contractor.

attributes.name: supervision_headcount
attributes.description: Number of supervisory personnel (foremen, superintendents, site managers) planned for the period.

attributes.name: support_staff_headcount
attributes.description: Number of support personnel (site engineers, QA/QC inspectors, safety officers, administrative staff) planned for the period.

attributes.name: total_planned_headcount
attributes.description: Total number of workers planned across all trades and roles for this staffing plan period, representing the aggregate workforce requirement.

attributes.name: total_planned_labor_hours
attributes.description: Total labor hours planned across all workers and trades for the planning period, used for cost estimation and productivity forecasting.

attributes.name: trade_mix_breakdown
attributes.description: Structured breakdown of planned headcount by trade category (e.g., 'Concrete:50|Steel:30|Electrical:25|Plumbing:20'), supporting trade-specific procurement and scheduling.

attributes.name: transportation_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether worker transportation (buses, flights, shuttles) is required for this staffing plan, impacting mobilization logistics and costs.

products.name: labor_rate
products.description: Reference record defining the all-in labor rates (base wage, fringe benefits, burden, overhead) for each trade classification under a specific labor agreement or project. Captures trade classification, effective date range, straight-time rate, overtime rate, double-time rate, fringe benefit rate, payroll burden percentage, and total loaded rate. Used for project cost estimation, bid pricing (BOQ), and job cost control.
products.reference: Prevailing Wage Rate / Loaded Labor Rate

attributes.name: cost_code_id
attributes.description: Reference to the labor cost code that categorizes this rate for job costing and financial reporting. Links to the WBS (Work Breakdown Structure) and SAP cost elements.

Linking labor_rate to client_framework_agreement enables rate

attributes.name: labor_cost_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.labor_cost_code. Business justification: Link labor_rate to labor_cost_code to associate each rate with its cost code definition, enabling removal of duplicate cost code attributes from labor_rate.

attributes.name: regulatory_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_obligation. attributes.name: apprentice_ratio
attributes.description: The maximum allowable ratio of apprentices to journeymen for this trade classification, as defined by union agreements or prevailing wage law (e.g., 1:3 means one apprentice per three journeymen). Nullable if not applicable.
attributes.references: Union Apprenticeship Standards, Prevailing Wage Apprentice Ratios

attributes.name: base_hourly_rate
attributes.description: The straight-time hourly wage rate paid to the worker for regular hours (typically up to 8 hours per day or 40 hours per week). Excludes fringe benefits and burden.
attributes.references: Davis-Bacon Wage Determinations, Union Wage Scales

attributes.name: certified_payroll_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rate is subject to certified payroll reporting requirements under prevailing wage law (True) or not (False). Used to trigger compliance workflows in HCSS HeavyJob and Viewpoint Vista.
attributes.references: Davis-Bacon Certified Payroll Requirements, State Prevailing Wage Compliance

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this labor rate record was first created in the source system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this record (e.g., USD, CAD, EUR, GBP). Required for multi-currency projects and international joint ventures.

attributes.name: double_time_hourly_rate
attributes.description: The hourly wage rate for double-time hours, typically 2.0x the base rate for hours worked on Sundays, holidays, or beyond a threshold (e.g., over 12 hours per day). Nullable if not applicable.
attributes.references: Union Collective Bargaining Agreements, State Overtime Laws

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which this labor rate expires or is superseded. Nullable for open-ended rates. Used to manage rate changes and contract renewals.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this labor rate becomes effective. Used for rate escalation tracking and historical cost analysis.

attributes.name: escalation_clause
attributes.description: Description of any contractual escalation provisions that adjust this rate over time (e.g., annual CPI adjustment, fixed percentage increase, renegotiation trigger). Nullable if no escalation applies.

attributes.name: fringe_benefit_rate
attributes.description: The hourly cost of fringe benefits (health insurance, pension, vacation, training funds, etc.) as defined by the labor agreement or prevailing wage determination. Added to base wage to calculate total compensation.
attributes.references: Davis-Bacon Fringe Benefits, Union Benefit Funds

attributes.name: jurisdiction

attributes.name: overtime_hourly_rate
attributes.description: The hourly wage rate for overtime hours, typically 1.5x the base rate for hours beyond 8 per day or 40 per week, as defined by labor agreements or prevailing wage law.

attributes.name: payroll_burden_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage markup applied to gross wages to cover employer-paid payroll taxes (FICA, FUTA, SUTA, workers compensation insurance, general liability insurance). Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 35.50 for 35.5%).

attributes.name: profit_margin_percentage

attributes.name: rate_code

attributes.name: shift_differential_rate

attributes.name: skill_level

products.name: trade_staffing_requirement
products.description: This association product represents the planned deployment of a specific construction trade within a specific staffing plan. It captures the trade-level workforce allocation — planned headcount, labor hours, ramp-up/ramp-down schedule, and peak demand — for each trade discipline required by a staffing plan. Each record links one staffing_plan to one skill_trade with attributes that exist only in the context of this trade-within-plan allocation. Recognized as a core workforce planning artifact in HCSS HeavyJob and SAP SuccessFactors.. Existence Justification: In construction workforce planning, a staffing plan is inherently a multi-trade document — a single project phase requires ironworkers, pipefitters, electricians, and carpenters simultaneously. The current model forces one staffing_plan record per trade (via a scalar skill_trade_id FK), which fragments what is operationally a single plan into multiple records. The correct model is a trade allocation record that captures planned headcount, labor hours, and schedule curves for each trade within a given staffing plan — a recognized artifact in HCSS HeavyJob and SAP SuccessFactors workforce planning.

products.name: lookahead_activity_commitment
products.description: This association product represents the Commitment between a CPM schedule activity and a short-interval lookahead plan within the Last Planner System (LPS). It captures the per-activity readiness state, constraint status, and commitment fulfillment for each activity as it appears in a specific rolling lookahead window. Each record links one activity to one lookahead_plan and carries readiness flags, constraint details, and window-specific planning dates that exist only in the context of this activity-plan pairing. This is the operational record that drives PPC (Percent Plan Complete) tracking and near-term crew coordination.. Existence Justification: In construction project controls, a CPM schedule activity can appear in multiple lookahead plans across successive rolling windows (e.g., an activity first appears in the 6-week window, then the 3-week window, then the 1-week window as it approaches execution). Conversely, each lookahead plan contains many activities. The Last Planner System explicitly models this as a commitment tracking mechanism where each activity-plan pairing carries its own readiness state (crew, materials, equipment confirmed), constraint status, and commitment fulfillment — data that belongs to neither the activity nor the plan alone.

products.name: activity_delay_impact
products.description: This association product represents the formal impact record between a delay_event and an activity in construction project controls. It captures the specific quantum of delay, critical path effect, and EOT entitlement for each activity affected by each delay event. Each record links one delay_event to one activity and carries attributes that exist only in the context of that specific event-activity impact relationship, supporting delay analysis methodologies (as-planned vs as-built, time impact analysis, windows analysis) per SCL Protocol and AACE RP 29R-03.. Existence Justification: In construction project controls, a single delay event (e.g., a severe weather event or a design change instruction) routinely impacts multiple schedule activities simultaneously, and a single activity can be impacted by multiple distinct delay events over its lifecycle. This is a formally managed operational relationship in delay analysis disciplines (SCL Protocol, AACE RP 29R-03): project controls engineers actively create, update, and close individual delay impact records per activity per event, tracking quantum of delay, critical path effect, and EOT entitlement at the activity level. The relationship is not derivable from existing transactional joins — it requires its own records with per-activity impact data.

products.name: inspection
products.description: Transactional record of a physical quality inspection or checklist verification event conducted on site, at a factory, or workshop. Captures inspection date, location, inspector identity, ITP line reference, checklist template used, item-level verification results (pass/fail/N/A per check item with remarks), overall outcome (pass/fail/conditional), observations, non-conformances raised, digital sign-off, and attachments (photos, measurements). Covers all inspection types: hold-point inspections, witness-point inspections, pre-pour checks, structural inspections, MEP inspections, and any checklist-based quality verification. domains.name: safety
domains.description: HSE (Health Safety Environment) domain managing incident reports, LTI (Lost Time Injury), TRIR (Total Recordable Incident Rate), near-miss records, SWMS (Safe Work Method Statements), PTW (Permit to Work), TBM (Toolbox Meeting) records, safety audits, corrective actions, PPE compliance, and environmental compliance records. Integrates with Intelex for incident management and OSHA/ISO 45001 regulatory reporting.

products.name: incident
products.description: Core master record for ALL HSE safety events on construction sites, encompassing the full severity spectrum: Lost Time Injuries (LTI), medical treatment cases (including body part affected, treatment type, treating physician, return-to-work date, fitness-for-duty status), first aid cases, restricted work cases, near-misses, unsafe conditions, behavioral safety observations, property damage, dangerous occurrences, and environmental events. Captures incident classification/type, severity, location (project/site/area), date/time, injured party details, immediate cause, root cause category, OSHA recordability flag, TRIR contribution, days away/restricted/transferred (DART), regulatory notification status, environmental media affected, and workers compensation claim reference. Serves as the single unified safety event register supporting OSHA 300/300A log generation, TRIR/LTIFR/DART rate calculations, leading indicator trending, and ISO 45001 reporting. Sourced from Intelex incident management module.

attributes.name: ppe_compliance
attributes.description: Indicates whether the injured party was wearing required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) at the time of the incident. Non-compliance is a key causal factor and triggers disciplinary and training corrective actions.

attributes.name: property_damage_amount

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_date

attributes.name: return_to_work_date

attributes.name: immediate_cause
attributes.description: Direct, observable cause of the incident — the unsafe act or unsafe condition that directly resulted in the event. Captured as a narrative description from the investigation findings.

attributes.name: incident_category

attributes.name: incident_classification

attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR 1904; ISO 45001:2018 Clause 10.2; ANSI Z16.1

attributes.name: incident_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the original Health Safety and Environment (HSE) incident occurred. Used as the principal business event date for regulatory reporting and trend analysis.

attributes.name: injured_party_type
attributes.description: Classification of the employment or affiliation status of the person(s) involved in the incident — distinguishing between direct employees, subcontractor workers, site visitors, or members of the public.

attributes.name: investigation_close_date
attributes.description: Date on which the investigation was formally closed following completion of root cause analysis, corrective action assignment, and management sign-off. Nullable until closure.

attributes.name: investigation_findings
attributes.description: Comprehensive narrative summary of all findings from the investigation, including evidence gathered, witness statements reviewed, site conditions observed, and conclusions drawn by the investigation team.
attributes.references: ISO 45001:2018 Clause 10.2; OSHA Incident Investigation Guidelines

attributes.name: investigation_methodology
attributes.description: Root cause analysis methodology applied during the investigation. Common methods include 5-Why analysis, Fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram, Bowtie analysis, Fault Tree Analysis, and TapRooT. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: 5_why|fishbone|bowtie|fault_tree|taproot|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ISO 45001:2018 Clause 10.2; OSHA Incident Investigation Guidelines

attributes.name: investigation_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric reference code assigned to the investigation, used in correspondence, regulatory submissions, and audit trails. Format: INV-YYYY-NNNNNN.

attributes.name: investigation_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which the formal investigation was initiated. Used to measure investigation response time and compliance with regulatory timelines for incident investigation commencement.

attributes.name: investigation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the incident investigation workflow, tracking progress from initial opening through root cause analysis, review, and formal closure.
attributes.references: ISO 45001:2018 Clause 10.2; Intelex Corrective Actions Module

attributes.name: investigation_team_members
attributes.description: Names and roles of all personnel who participated in the investigation team, including the lead investigator, HSE representative, site supervisor, and any subject matter experts. Stored as a structured text list.

attributes.name: investigation_type
attributes.description: Classification of the investigation scope and formality level. Formal investigations are conducted for Lost Time Injuries (LTI), fatalities, and high-potential incidents. Informal investigations cover minor incidents and near-misses.

attributes.name: is_lti
attributes.description: Indicates whether the incident resulted in a Lost Time Injury (LTI), defined as any work-related injury or illness that results in at least one full day away from work beyond the day of the incident.

attributes.name: is_recordable
attributes.description: Indicates whether the incident meets OSHA recordability criteria and must be entered on the OSHA 300 Log. Recordable incidents include work-related fatalities, injuries, and illnesses meeting specific severity thresholds.

attributes.name: is_regulatory_reportable
attributes.description: Indicates whether the incident requires mandatory notification to a regulatory authority such as OSHA, EPA, or local government within a prescribed timeframe (e.g., OSHA requires fatality reporting within 8 hours).
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR 1904.39; EPA Regulations; ISO 45001:2018 Clause 10.2

attributes.name: lessons_learned
attributes.description: Key lessons identified from the investigation that should be communicated across the organisation and other project sites to prevent similar incidents. Used in Toolbox Meeting (TBM) communications and safety alerts.

attributes.name: lost_time_days
attributes.description: Number of calendar days lost due to the incident as determined by the investigation. Used in calculating Lost Time Injury (LTI) frequency rates and Total Recordable Incident Rate (TRIR) for OSHA regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: management_review_date
attributes.description: Date on which senior management formally reviewed and accepted the investigation report and corrective action plan. Required for ISO 45001 management review compliance.

attributes.name: ppe_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the injured party was wearing the required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) at the time of the incident. Non-compliance is a key contributing factor captured in the investigation.

attributes.name: recurrence_prevention_measures
attributes.description: Narrative description of specific engineering controls, administrative controls, or procedural changes recommended to prevent recurrence of the incident type. Aligned with the hierarchy of controls.
attributes.references: ISO 45001:2018 Clause 8.1.2; OSHA Hierarchy of Controls

attributes.name: regulatory_reference_number
attributes.description: Reference or case number assigned by the regulatory authority (e.g., OSHA case number) upon submission of the incident report. Used for tracking regulatory correspondence and compliance status.

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_date
attributes.description: Date on which the incident investigation report or notification was formally submitted to the relevant regulatory authority (e.g., OSHA, EPA). Nullable for non-reportable incidents.

attributes.name: root_cause_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative of the fundamental systemic root cause(s) identified through the investigation methodology (e.g., 5-Why, Fishbone). Represents the deepest causal factor that, if corrected, would prevent recurrence.

attributes.name: swms_in_place_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Safe Work Method Statement (SWMS) In Place Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a valid Safe Work Method Statement (SWMS) was in place and accessible for the work activity being performed at the time of the incident. Absence of SWMS is a key systemic cause indicator.

attributes.name: systemic_cause
attributes.description: Organisational or management system failure that allowed the immediate and root causes to exist, such as inadequate procedures, insufficient training, or failed management controls. Distinct from immediate and root causes.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the incident investigation record. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking for regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: ISO 45001:2018 Clause 7.5; GDPR Article 5(2); ISO 9001:2015 Clause 7.5

attributes.name: witness_count
attributes.description: Number of witnesses interviewed during the investigation. Indicates the breadth of evidence gathering and supports completeness assessment of the investigation.
attributes.references: ISO 45001:2018 Clause 10.2; OSHA Incident Investigation Guidelines

attributes.name: work_area_description
attributes.description: Specific work area, zone, or location within the construction site where the incident occurred, such as excavation zone, scaffolding level, electrical room, or crane operating radius.

attributes.name: emergency_procedures

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The date after which the SWMS is no longer valid for use and must be re-approved or superseded. Distinct from review_date — expiry renders the document invalid, whereas review_date triggers a re-assessment.

attributes.name: hazard_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of all identified hazards associated with the high-risk activity, including physical, chemical, biological, ergonomic, and environmental hazards. Captured as a consolidated summary at the SWMS header level.

attributes.name: initial_risk_consequence
attributes.description: Consequence severity rating of the identified hazard before any control measures are applied (inherent risk). Combined with initial_risk_likelihood to produce the initial risk rating score.
attributes.references: ISO 45001:2018 Clause 6.1.2; AS/NZS 4360 Risk Management Standard

attributes.name: initial_risk_likelihood
attributes.description: Likelihood rating of the identified hazard materialising before any control measures are applied (inherent risk). Used in conjunction with initial_risk_consequence to derive the initial risk rating per the risk matrix.
attributes.references: ISO 45001:2018 Clause 6.1.2; AS/NZS 4360 Risk Management Standard

attributes.name: initial_risk_rating
attributes.description: Overall risk rating derived from the combination of initial_risk_likelihood and initial_risk_consequence before any control measures are applied. Represents the inherent risk level of the activity.
attributes.references: ISO 45001:2018 Clause 6.1.2; AS/NZS 4360; Intelex Risk Matrix

attributes.name: intelex_record_reference

attributes.name: issue_date

attributes.name: last_reviewed_date

attributes.name: plant_equipment_required

attributes.name: ppe_requirements

attributes.name: ptw_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Permit to Work (PTW) must be issued and active before the activity described in this SWMS can commence. True for activities such as confined space entry, hot works, and electrical isolation.

attributes.name: ptw_type
attributes.description: Type of Permit to Work (PTW) required in conjunction with this SWMS. Populated only when ptw_required is True. Drives the PTW issuance workflow in Intelex.

attributes.name: residual_risk_consequence
attributes.description: Consequence severity rating after all control measures have been applied. Combined with residual_risk_likelihood to produce the residual risk rating.
attributes.references: ISO 45001:2018 Clause 6.1.2; AS/NZS 4360 Risk Management Standard

attributes.name: residual_risk_likelihood
attributes.description: Likelihood rating of the hazard materialising after all control measures have been applied. Used to assess the effectiveness of controls and determine if the residual risk is acceptable.
attributes.references: ISO 45001:2018 Clause 6.1.2; AS/NZS 4360 Risk Management Standard

attributes.name: residual_risk_rating
attributes.description: Overall risk rating after all control measures have been applied. Represents the residual risk level that must be accepted or further mitigated before work can proceed. Extreme residual risk requires escalation to HSE Manager.
attributes.references: ISO 45001:2018 Clause 6.1.2; AS/NZS 4360; Intelex Risk Matrix

attributes.name: review_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date by which the SWMS must be reviewed and re-validated for continued applicability. Triggers review workflow in Intelex when the date is reached or when site conditions change materially.

attributes.name: revision_number
attributes.description: Sequential revision number of the SWMS document, incremented each time the document is formally revised and re-approved. Revision 0 represents the initial issue.

attributes.name: swms_number

attributes.description: Indicates whether all workers performing the activity must sign the SWMS to confirm they have read, understood, and agree to comply with the documented procedures and controls.
